By quantifying their divergence from human populations in terms of emotional expression, we hope that our methods can aid in this effort.

title: Geometric Control of Electronic Decoherence in a Chiral Spin-Orbit Coupled Helix
authors: Neel Moudgal, Nicholas A. Kotov, Eitan Geva
abstract: While chirality is known to impact chemical and optical properties of molecular systems, as well as their biological function, far less is known about its impact on quantum coherence. By considering a chiral helix as a paradigmatic model, we show that within the Born-Markov regime, changing the degree of helical twist can be used to modulate the electronic decoherence rate. Moderate to strong spin-orbit coupling between next-nearest-neighbor sites along the helix are shown to give rise to a strong dependence of the electronic decoherence rate on the degree of chirality. The effect of chirality on electronic decoherence rates is also seen to be strongly impacted by the spatial and temporal correlations between the local environmental fluctuations to which the local excitations along the helix are subject. Our results show that chirality can serve as a tunable design parameter for quantum engineering and highlight the importance role environmental correlations can play in determining how chirality affects electronic decoherence rates.

title: Analytic properties of distributions associated with multi-state Random Number Generators
authors: Douglas T. Pfeffer, Volodymyr Zabolotnyi
abstract: We analyze the analytic properties of probability distributions associated with possibly unfair, multi-state Random Number Generators (i.e., dice). Specifically, given a $q$-sided die, if $x_i\in \{0,\ldots, q-1\}$ denotes the outcome of the $i^{\text{th}}$ toss, then $F(x)=\mathbb{P}[X\leq x]$ is the associated cumulative distribution function---a probabilistic generalization of the famed Cantor function. We first establish easily computable bounds for the $L^1$-distance between the possibly unfair $F$ and the uniform distribution $y=x$. We then show that $F$ is both upper- and lower-Hölder continuous, where the associated Hölder exponents are shown to be sharp. Finally, we establish recursive formulae for the moments, $\mathbb{E}[X^n]$, associated with $F$ and use these moments to provide sequences of step-functions that converge uniformly to $F$ from above and below.

title: Background characterization in the PIKACHU Phase 1 search for two-neutrino double-beta decay of $^{160}$Gd
authors: T. Omori, T. Iida, A. Gando, N. Hinohara, K. Hosokawa, S. Ishidate, M. Ishigami, T. Kishimoto, K. Mizukoshi, T. Sako, S. Sugi, M. Yoshino, K. Fushimi, K. Kamada, Y. Shoji, Y. Suga, H. Suzuki, K. Takahashi
abstract:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2β$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. The experimental backgrounds were investigated through delayed-coincidence analysis and spectral fitting based on GEANT4 simulations. In particular, surface contamination of the crystal was identified through the characteristic distortion of the $^{214}$Po $α$-ray spectrum, leading to an improved background model that reproduces the observed energy spectra. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2ν}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay.

title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control
authors: Jeong Woon Lee, Namho Kim, Hyoseok Hwang
abstract: Actor-critic methods achieve high returns in robotic control, yet trained actors exhibit high-frequency action oscillations. Most smoothness methods constrain the actor, whereas PAVE regularizes the critic by separately penalizing action-gradient variation and encouraging negative action curvature. The same gradient change, however, moves the critic's preferred action farther where the critic is flat, and separate penalties do not measure this motion. We characterize this motion through the greedy shift, which approximates greedy-action displacement across state transitions to first order under local concavity. Since displacement alone does not reflect its critic-value consequences, the analysis further shows that the shift's curvature-weighted energy approximates the value lost by retaining the previous greedy action to second order. Based on this relationship, POISE regularizes the curvature-weighted energy along temporal and spatial state displacements. It employs a saddle-free curvature metric and reward-scale-consistent scaling while leaving the actor unchanged. On six continuous control tasks with TD3, POISE reduces the smoothness score on every task by $5.9\times$ on average ($4.5\times$ geometric mean), compared with $2.2\times$ ($1.9\times$) for the strongest baseline, and achieves the lowest score on five tasks. Paired return intervals include zero on four tasks, with a 14% increase on Ant and an 11% decrease on Hopper.

title: Breaking the Square-Root Space Barrier for Longest Increasing Subsequence
authors: Naohito Matsumoto, Masashi Kiyomi
abstract: For every fixed constant $\varepsilon>0$, we give deterministic algorithms for computing the length of a longest increasing subsequence (LIS) and for outputting an LIS in input order, both in $O(n^{2+\varepsilon})$ time and $O(\sqrt n/2^{δ\sqrt{\log n}})={\rm o}(\sqrt n)$ bits of working space for some constant $δ>0$. The input is read-only and the output is write-only. This answers an open question of Kiyomi et al. Our construction combines small-pile skipping with recursive blockwise computation of pile tops. Balanced reconstruction uses streaming intersections of forward and backward piles.

title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
authors: Zihao Wu, Qi Zhang
abstract: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

title: GaokaoMathGen: Chinese Gaokao Mathematics Finale Problem Generation Controlled by Latent Reasoning Structures
authors: Qian Chen, Kun Zhu, Zhongyi Wang, Ling Chen
abstract: Generating Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problems requires controlling not only the included skills, but also the underlying mathematical kernel and solution path. Existing LLM-based methods mainly rely on surface-level specifications, while the realized difficulty of generated problems cannot be determined directly from prompted targets. Therefore, we propose GaokaoMathGen, a framework for Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problem generation controlled by latent reasoning structures. It extracts standardized latent reasoning structures from seed problems and performs constrained synthesis using skills, methods, a core identity, and a pivot step as structural controls. We further estimate realized difficulty through logical-quality filtering, fixed-solver decoding effort, structural features, and solver-output search signals. Experiments show that semantic normalization improves cross-annotator comparability and that 78.0% of 609 scored candidates pass the logical-quality filter. In a teacher audit of the 60 highest-effort candidates, all were judged to reach finale or penultimate problem difficulty, and only one exhibited a severe logical issue. These results support latent reasoning structures as effective control signals for generating high-difficulty mathematical problems.

title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
authors: Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Shicheng Cao, Xing Nie, Xiaopeng Yu, Ke Dong, Zijie Zhao, Shenling Qiu, Yizhao Xu, Feiyang Xue, Haonan Liu, Haoyu Zhang, Haobo Jia, Zheng Liu, Anqi Yang, Jiahui Niu, Yue Sun, Tailai Cheng, Jianpeng Yu, Yang Wen, Longhao Wei, Zibin Dong, Shiduo Zhang, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao
abstract: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging.

title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
authors: Huajun Huang
abstract: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields. Over fields with more than two elements, exact preservation of rank \(k\) implies rank-\(k\) nonincrease. Over \(\F_2\), for each \(k\ge2\), we construct a rank-\(k\) preserver that sends a rank-one matrix to a matrix of rank \(k+1\). For maps whose images have upper rank \(k\), three block rank equalities characterize exact preservation. Over \(\C\), we combine the Huang--Landsberg classification with a degree obstruction on \(\mathrm{PGL}_k\) to show that every primitive core of upper rank four arising from a rank-four preserver is, up to equivalence and transposition, a projected exterior-product space on \(\C^5\). If either source dimension exceeds five, every complex rank-four preserver is standard with full-rank factors or is a compression. A \(4\times5\) example attains the bound. The degree obstruction also shows that, over any algebraically closed field, every linear map \(\M_k\to\Alt_{k+1}\) sends some invertible matrix to a matrix of rank at most \(k-2\) when \(4\mid k\).

title: Temporal Soliton Waves in Modern Fiber Laser Systems
authors: Shilong Liu, Boris Malomed
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of temporal soliton-wave in modern fiber systems. Temporal soliton waves constitute a broad class of nonlinear localized structures in modern fiber laser systems, arising from different balances among dispersion, nonlinearity, gain, loss, spectral filtering, and various forms of cavity coupling. We review the underlying theory, basic experimental findings, and practical methods for the generation, real-time characterization, and active control of soliton families, with a particular focus on recent progress reported for mode-locked fiber-laser platforms. The families covered in the chapter include dissipative solitons, soliton molecules (bound states), and dispersion-managed solitons. For each species, we focus on the pulse energy, duration, stationary and breathing states, and emerging intelligent (machine-learning-assisted) control strategies.

title: A short proof of Serre positivity
authors: Linquan Ma
abstract: Recently, OpenAI found a proof of the positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity. The two main ingredients are a descent result on rational $K$-theory with support; and a construction of certain category of asymptotic complexes that identifies with the category of perfect complexes over a connective (non-commutative) derived ring. In this article, we present a simpler proof of Serre positivity that circumvents the second step; instead, we use a ``reduction to the diagonal" trick via the $A_{\text{inf}}$-construction.

title: SwarmLeak: Does Coordination Improve Privacy Attacks on LLM Agents?
authors: Asma Farajidizaji, Vyas Raina, Vatsal Raina, Ivaxi Sheth
abstract: LLM agents increasingly collaborate in group chats while holding tool access to confidential records, which makes the shared chat an attack surface. It remains unclear whether several colluding attackers extract such information more effectively than one. We introduce SwarmLeak, a red-teaming dataset of 24 synthetic group-chat scenarios across healthcare, law, finance, and software engineering, where attackers pose as colleagues to make a victim agent post protected fields despite an explicit confidentiality policy. With GLM 5.2 attacking five victim models through seven conversational strategies, we compare one attacker with a swarm of four sharing a private channel, matching scenarios, strategies, and a 200,000-token budget that also covers swarm coordination. Swarms show no advantage: a single attacker matches or exceeds them on every victim, and the share of runs leaking any field differs between conditions by at most 14.3 percentage points, whereas changing the victim shifts it from 0% to 99.4%. On the two most vulnerable models, nearly every run leaks under both conditions, but single attackers expose more of the record at first disclosure (85.4% vs. 68.1% of protected fields on Nemotron 3.5 Lightning). Four of the five victims leaked despite the policy. GLM 5.2 retrieved protected data in 64.3% of individual-attack runs and leaked in 0.6%: retrieval does not imply disclosure, but in high-stakes settings even one leaked field can identify a patient or client. At equal budgets, a larger red team is not automatically a stronger one; the victim model matters far more.

title: Many Senses, One World: Learning Hierarchical Multimodal World Representations for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
authors: Jin Yang, Youlin Wang, Ping Wei
abstract: Bimanual dexterous manipulation relies on multimodal inputs that capture visual context and non-visual physical interaction cues for precise and coordinated control. To address the challenge of effectively integrating these modalities for policy learning, we propose HiMoDex, a two-stage framework centered on hierarchical multimodal world-state representations. In Stage 1, we pretrain a hierarchical representation network on the collected dataset of 1.19 million synchronized multimodal time steps. The network integrates visual context with tactile, force-torque, and audio cues into unified world-state embeddings. In Stage 2, we freeze the pretrained network and use its embeddings to condition a shared world-action transformer. The transformer jointly learns action generation and action-conditioned future-state prediction. Experiments across five real-world tasks show that HiMoDex achieves an average success rate of 78.7\%, representing an absolute improvement of 32.0\% over the strongest evaluated baseline. Extensive ablations validate the benefits of hierarchical representation learning and two-stage training. Failure analysis helps explain performance differences across variants. Code, data, and demos will be released at https://anonymous.4open.science/w/research-website-BAB4/.

title: Joint Trajectory and Power Optimization for Movable-Antenna-Aided Secure Transmission
authors: Jiacheng Liao, Fengchao Zhu, Guojie Hu, Ying Zhang, Tong-Xing Zheng
abstract: This paper investigates joint trajectory and power optimization for movable antenna (MA)-aided secure transmission, where the MA can transmit during its movement. Specifically, the average secrecy rate is maximized subject to movement and power constraints, which couple the MA positions and transmit powers over time, respectively. To tackle this nonconvex problem, we first decouple the transmit powers via Lagrangian duality, where the optimal power for a given trajectory is derived in semi-closed form and shown to depend only on the current MA position. Accordingly, we decouple the MA positions by equivalently reformulating the problem on a discretized linear rail in terms of the farthest grid point and the number of time slots spent at each grid point. Then, from strong duality of the convex relaxation for each farthest point, we construct an asymptotically optimal solution in which the MA dwells at no more than two positions. Finally, a low-complexity dual-based branch-and-bound algorithm is developed to select the farthest grid point and certify the optimality gap. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms the benchmark schemes.

title: Probing the inner structure of bound states
authors: Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, Karl Jansen
abstract: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.

title: Separating Measurement Failures from Defence Failures in Split Language-Model Privacy
authors: Georgios Politis, Evangelos Pappas
abstract: Split-training privacy evaluations fail through distinct mechanisms. Evaluators can overlook an exposed gradient channel, align reconstructions against shifted labels, or deploy uncalibrated probes before testing a candidate defence, while calibrated attacks can also refute real defences. Separating these failure modes alters which claims survive. We conduct a retrospective evidentiary reanalysis across four split-LLM campaigns and two cross-cutting scope checks covering host key custody and variational mutual-information bounds, mapping every recorded claim to one of five admissibility states (breach, non-detection, undetermined coverage, invalid measurement, or out-of-scope inference). Across a 19-configuration exploration, only four of 24 required probes qualified, yet those four calibrated probes still established qualified privacy breaches in 13 configurations, while utility or learning-gain failures eliminated the remaining 6. In a seven-cell defence-redesign pilot, 2 quantised configurations failed utility gates, calibrated next-byte structure probes breached the 0.02 gate on all 7 cells (0.097 to 0.112), and qualified punctuation-property probes reached 0.79 to 0.89, yielding 4 failed and 3 undetermined composite privacy assessments (the latter from marginal null-band excursions on punctuation bindings). Negative evidence against both defence families remains intact. Scope checks further show that shared-key orthogonal wrappers protect passive network captures without hiding activations from a compromised restoring host, and why near-zero variational lower bounds leave worst-case leakage unconstrained. Rerunnable scripts verify 1,522 checks across 122 SHA-256-pinned artifacts while preserving each campaign's native seed intervals and retrospective boundaries.

title: MOSAIC: Memory-Organized Search with Anti-Imitation Crossover for Training-Free Microarchitecture Optimization
authors: Kaushal Mhapsekar, Bita Aslrousta, Paula Contreras, Azam Ghanbari, Samira Mirbagher Ajorpaz
abstract: Large language models can generate cache-replacement policies. The central challenge is to retain performance on workloads excluded from the search. In our adaptations of published search methods, generated code resembles established policies, with cosine similarities of 0.78-0.84. The wider comparison also shows held-out harmonic-mean instructions-per-cycle (IPC) losses of 1.0-2.4%. We present MOSAIC, a search controller that improves policies without updating language-model weights. It stores concise lessons from previous evaluations rather than repeatedly copying high-scoring code. When improvement stops, it selects two high-scoring policies whose code embeddings differ and asks the model to combine their mechanisms. Novelty prompts and model rotation support this search; controlled memory edits test how the stored lessons affect later proposals. We evaluate cache replacement using intervention-level cross-validation and a wider comparison on ten memory-intensive SPEC2006 workloads. MOSAIC reaches a 51.1% peak hit rate on the primary search workload and a 47.9% held-out mean in the intervention study. Removing crossover reduces these values by 7.8 and 21.8 percentage points, respectively, whereas the tested stronger model improves the held-out mean by 0.4 points. In the wider IPC comparison, MOSAIC has the smallest held-out gap (0.31%) and the highest held-out IPC among the evaluated LLM configurations. Adapting the same controller to data prefetching gives a 4.8% mean speedup over the LRU reference configuration. The accompanying corpus contains 10,687 generated policies with lineage and per-iteration prompt logs.

title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program
authors: Maria Eduarda Pinheiro, Vitoria Caroline Blau
abstract: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.

title: Cardinal Transfer Events for Infinitary Logic with Infinitary Quantification
authors: Edgar Valenzuela
abstract: Assuming the existence of a certain theory $Φ$, we solve the Gap-$n$ problem for more than one predicate. This will be done for infinitary logic with infinitary quantification.

title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming for Robot Foundation Models
authors: Kyle Coelho, Eugen Solowjow
abstract: This paper demonstrates an approach for correcting failures of robot foundation models (RFMs) without additional data collection, demonstrations, or training. We apply weight-space programming (WSP), in which a language-model agent directly reads and writes a neural network's parameters, to a large, pre-trained vision-language-action policy. The idea is simple: many policy failures are not random but repeatedly land in the same recognizable stuck state, so if that state is visible in the model's internal activations, a small edit could trigger a corrective movement while leaving the rest of the model's parameters unchanged. A core design choice is where to write the edit: repurposing a few near-silent neurons in the action expert lets the edit switch on in situations associated with the failure and produce a corrective movement, such as lowering the gripper toward the target, that is specified directly rather than learned through training. Empirically, when applied to the pi0.5 policy in simulation, we find that edits to roughly 0.0002% of the parameters can improve success on recurring failures, including for a policy that was already fine-tuned on its task. Reversed and random edits indicate that the gains come from the intended behavior, and the approach works best when the failure situation is recognizable and a simple correction can address it.

title: Sum rules for the relativistic and retarded Bethe approximation in electron-neutral-atom collisions
authors: Colm T. Whelan
abstract: For high partial waves the reactance matrix for electron-atom collisions may be replaced by the Bethe approximation, and for optically allowed transitions the slowly convergent sum over partial waves can then be performed exactly by means of the sum rules of Burgess. For neutral targets the Bethe integrals and the sum rules take a particularly simple form in terms of Legendre functions of the second kind of a single argument $χ=(k^2+k'^2)/2kk'$. We show that this structure survives in a fully relativistic description. For a projectile described by free Dirac waves interacting through the retarded Møller interaction, the Bethe integrals of every multipole order are obtained from the static ones by the replacement $χ\toχ_q=(k^2+k'^2-q^2)/2kk'$, where $q$ is the energy transfer divided by $c$. For dipole transitions we give closed-form sum rules over all partial waves above any $l_0\ge2$ for the Coulomb (charge-density) interaction, for the magnetic dipole interaction and for the long-range transverse electric interaction, including its interference with the Coulomb term. In each case the sum reduces to a quadratic form in $Q_{l_0-1}(χ_q)$ and $Q_{l_0}(χ_q)$ with coefficients rational in $l_0$. As the impact energy increases $χ_q\to1$ and the partial-wave sums converge ever more slowly, so that the sum rules become most useful precisely in the relativistic regime.

title: Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
authors: Andrés Laín Sanclemente
abstract: After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.

title: Time-uniform bounds and long-time asymptotics for a three-species drift-diffusion model for memristors
authors: Ansgar Jüngel, Tuan Tung Nguyen
abstract: The qualitative behavior of weak solutions to the two-dimensional drift-diffusion equations for memristors, incorporating Shockley-Read-Hall-type generation-recombination terms and time-dependent boundary conditions, is investigated. The model couples the electron, hole, and oxygen-vacancy densities to the electric potential through the Poisson equation. The global existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established. If the boundary data converge to the thermal equilibrium at an integrable rate, the densities remain uniformly-in-time bounded above and below, and the solution converges exponentially fast to thermal equilibrium. For time-independent boundary data and sufficiently small applied bias, solutions converge exponentially fast to steady states carrying nonzero fluxes.

title: TESS: Query-Guided Temporal Event-Structured Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding
authors: Qi Lu, Shiyan Tong, Shujie Li, Sen Li, Likun shi, Maofei Que, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu
abstract: Temporal localization in long videos is challenging because brief, question-relevant events are dispersed among extensive redundant content. Limited visual budgets increase the risk of omitting these events or their temporal context, undermining reliable reasoning. Existing frame selection methods emphasize semantic relevance or temporal coverage, often overlooking the complementary evidence needed to locate related events and establish their temporal relationships. To address this limitation, we propose TESS, a training-free framework for query-guided temporal event-structured frame selection. TESS selects frames that jointly show the reference event and the event asked about, in the required temporal order. Leveraging frozen vision-language representations, TESS integrates soft temporal gating, role-aware budget allocation, and within-role redundancy suppression to preserve complementary event evidence. Extensive experiments across four long-video understanding benchmarks and three multimodal backbones demonstrate that TESS consistently outperforms the strongest compared baseline by 4.0-5.5 percentage points under a fixed frame budget. Further analyses reveal greater improvements on longer videos and robust performance under tighter visual budgets, while independent evidence annotations confirm enhanced event and temporal-relation coverage. These findings establish explicit temporal evidence organization as an effective training-free strategy for preserving event relationships and supporting efficient temporal reasoning over long videos. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TESS_code.

title: Noncommutative $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed beta functions of first and second kind : beta gamma relations, shift identities and symmetrisation
authors: Kawèyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph Désiré Bukweli Kyemba
abstract: We develop the theory of the beta functions attached to the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba, for structure functions whose deformed numbers are generated by two deformation functions $φ_{1}>φ_{2}>0$. Working with the Jackson type series representation of the deformed integral, we define a first kind beta function on $[0,1]$ from the deformed power $(1\ominusφ_{2}t)^{y-1}$, extended to complex exponents, and a second kind beta function on the half line from $(1\oplusφ_{1}t)^{-x-y}$. The first kind function equals $φ_{1}^{(y-1)(2x+y-2)/2}Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x)Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(y)/Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x+y)$ for all complex arguments with positive real parts; we derive its general shift identity, its exchange defect $φ_{1}^{(y-x)(x+y-1)/2}$, a commutative symmetrisation unique up to a constant, its asymptotics and a deformed Euler integral for a deformed Gauss hypergeometric function, which yields a deformed Gauss summation. The second kind function is evaluated through Ramanujan's ${}_{1}ψ_{1}$ summation and involves a second deformed gamma function, differing from the first one by a one periodic theta quotient, so that its exchange defect persists in the one parameter case. We prove a Bohr Mollerup type characterisation and a multiplication formula for the deformed gamma function, show that it is logarithmically convex on the positive half line if and only if $φ_{1}\geq1$, obtain the joint logarithmic convexity of normalised beta functions with a deformed Turán identity, and compute the moments of the associated deformed beta distributions. Gauge invariance covers the Jagannathan Srinivasa Rao, Chakrabarti Jagannathan, generalized $q-$Quesne and Hounkonnou Ngompe deformations, and every identity is confirmed numerically to thirty digits.

title: Contribution to the GdTe$_3$ magnetic phase diagram from electronic transport measurements
authors: A. A. Sinchenko, P. D. Grigoriev, A. Hadj-Azzem, E. Pachoud, E. Lorenzo, P. Monceau
abstract: Magnetic phase diagrams of the three antiferromagnetic (AFM) transitions of GdTe$_3$ that occur at zero magnetic field at $T_{N1}=12$ K, $T_{N2}=10.5$ K and $T_1=7$ K are investigated by means of resistance measurements in a magnetic field oriented along the three crystallographic directions. With the magnetic field applied in the basal plane we found re-entrance of an intermediate phase which may be a result of the coupling between the $T_{N2}$ AFM and the charge density wave with possibly a ferroaxial order. A spin flop transition is also observed at a temperature that presumably converges towards a triple point in vicinity of 2.5-3.0 T and $T$ between $T_1$ and $T_{N2}$. Our results help complete a complex phase diagram of GdTe$_3$ and advance a method for investigating magnetic ordering via transport measurements -- a technique applicable to many other compounds.

title: Evolve to Learn: Gradient-aligned experience evolution for model self-improvement
authors: Haoyuan Li, Gangyi Zhang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Daoxuan Liu, Jiancan Wu, Shiu-hong Kao, Wu Liu, Yicong Li, Yongdong Zhang
abstract: Self-evolving language models can continuously acquire useful experience through test-time interaction, reflection, and prompt optimization, yet turning such experience into model itself to ensure self improvement remains challenging. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides a natural mechanism for internalizing test-time information into model parameters, yet it largely assumes that the gener- ated experience is worth learning. We show that this assumption does not always hold: experiences that improve test-time performance may provide limited or even harmful training signals. To better characterize which experience should be inter- nalized, we systematically analyze diverse mutated experiences across multiple tasks and reflection models, and find that gradient-based alignment is a more reli- able indicator of downstream distillation gains than immediate test-time improve- ment. Based on this finding, we propose E2L, a self-evolution framework that iteratively generates, evaluates, and distills experiences according to their esti- mated training utility. E2L closes the loop between experience generation and parameter learning, enabling agents to autonomously produce experience suitable for self-improvement.

title: Found in Translation: Five Entry Points to Translate AI Literacy Frameworks in the Design of Educational Materials
authors: Luis Morales-Navarro, Karl-Emil K. Bilstrup, Mille Skovhus Lunding, Luke Connelly, Ane V. Jensen, Maja Dybboe, Yasmin B. Kafai, Marianne Graves Petersen, Ole Sejer Iversen
abstract: While there is a plethora of AI literacy and informatics frameworks, in practice it is difficult for designers of educational materials and educators to decide where to start and how to use these in learning activities. At the same time, recent reviews show that despite the fact that most frameworks emphasize the socio-technical nature of AI, in practice interventions tend to center on preparing learners to use AI. To address these issues, we ask: How can multiple stakeholders negotiate and translate AI literacy framework ideas into common language that can be used to design introductory learning materials for primary school children, teachers and parents? We introduce five entry points into AI literacy that were developed from a computational empowerment perspective through a participatory design process involving primary teacher educators, curricular designers, media producers, and researchers. We present three vignettes that illustrate how the entry points were generative in the design of learning activities, learning tools and media content for school and home. This paper contributes an account of the participatory development of five entry points that serve as generative and negotiable resources for designing educational materials.

title: DBFM: Dual-Band Flow Matching for ECG Super-Resolution
authors: Fan-Yi Hsu, Kuan-Chen Wang, I Chiu, Kai-Chun Liu, Ping-Cheng Yeh, Yu Tsao
abstract: Long-term ECG monitoring is increasingly supported by wearable and portable devices, where limited power and transmission capacity motivate acquisition at lower sampling rates. ECG super-resolution (SR) aims to reconstruct high-sampling-rate signals from low-sampling-rate recordings for clinical analysis. A recent diffusion-based approach, DiSR-ECG, has demonstrated powerful reconstruction performance, particularly in cross-dataset evaluation. However, its iterative sampling during inference incurs high computational cost when processing large volumes of long-term ECG data. To reduce this cost while maintaining reconstruction accuracy, we propose Dual-Band Flow Matching (DBFM), a generative framework for ECG SR. DBFM decomposes ECG signals into low- and high-frequency components and separately learns their source-to-target transport using conditional flow matching. This dual-band formulation enables frequency-specific reconstruction, while one-step inference substantially reduces computational complexity. Experimental results show that DBFM achieves performance comparable to or better than DiSR-ECG while reducing inference FLOPs by approximately 98.7\%. These results demonstrate that DBFM enables computationally efficient ECG SR without compromising reconstruction quality.

title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
authors: Miguel A. L. Marques, Irene D'Amico, Stefano Pittalis
abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.

title: Visual-State Graph Memory for Streaming Video Understanding
authors: Ailar Mahdizadeh, Pritam Sarkar, Xiangteng He, Leonid Sigal
abstract: In streaming video understanding, the evidence needed to answer a question may have already left the recent-frame window. Keeping all frames does not scale with video length, while dropping older frames limits the model's ability to reason about the past. We propose Visual-State Graph (VSG), a training-free memory that stores the state of a stream rather than the raw sequence of frames. VSG represents the stream as a graph of objects and their relations, together with a log of events; similar to a dynamically evolving scene graph. An object observed repeatedly is represented by one persistent node, with a timestamped history of how its state changes. To determine whether a newly mentioned object already exists in the graph, we compare the relations it takes part in with those of stored objects. We build this memory as the video arrives, before the questions are known. When a question arrives, we retrieve relevant objects and events alongside recent frames under a fixed input budget. Our evaluation spans four streaming-video benchmarks and seven open-source vision-language models ranging from 7B to 32B parameters. Under matched input budgets, VSG improves reasoning about the past while preserving real-time understanding.

title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
authors: Xintong Jiang
abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let \((X,B)\) be a projective log canonical pair with \(X\) of Fano type, \(-(K_X+B)\) nef and coefficients of \(B\) in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all \(ε\)-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of \(ε\). We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral \(\Q\)-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.

title: Protective-Design Pre-Emption in Child-Facing Generative AI
authors: Verena Jasmin Hallitschke, Mahelie Dissanayake, Elisa Nguyen
abstract: Generative AI is adopted rapidly by children, yet unrestricted general-audience models dominate their usage. This paper presents the open problem of \emph{protective-design pre-emption}: Delayed market introduction, low access thresholds, utility gaps, habituation, and peer adoption foster unrestricted AI model lock-in, leading children to bypass child-centric platforms. With first signs of lower adoption of child-centric platforms, we argue that this shift may reinforce existing AI risks such as exposing children to deepened parasocial dependencies, skill erosion, and misinformation. To address this problem, we propose interdisciplinary research directions to quantify pre-emption, understand its socio-technical drivers, and develop interventions ensuring child-centric AI is actively adopted, not just available.

title: Beyond Hard Tokens: Predictive Memory for Multimodal Protein Generation
authors: Xiaoliang Shi, Zichen Wang, Zhijian Wei, Zhanpeng Shi, Zhenghong Zhou, Yunpeng Wang, Shuangjia Zheng
abstract: Multimodal protein language models unify sequence and discrete structural tokens via iterative masked decoding, offering a promising paradigm for joint protein design. However, standard decoders rely on a memoryless mask reset at each iteration: only a sparse subset of newly committed hard tokens is carried forward, while all remaining unresolved sites are reset to an identical [MASK] embedding. In open-ended co-generation where neither modality provides a fixed external anchor, this stateless transition limits single-step refinement depth and deprives both tracks of stable cross-step soft anchors, leading to slow convergence or degenerative repetitive collapse. Observing that uncommitted predictions evolve with pronounced temporal coherence rather than erratic noise, we introduce Predictive Memory (PredMem), a training-free self-conditioning recurrence that carries these soft beliefs across steps. At each step, PredMem summarizes raw logits into a probability-weighted Top-$k$ expectation embedding at every residue and affinely interpolates it into eligible masked inputs on the next step at zero extra denoiser cost. Across DPLM-2, DPLM-2.1, and ESM3, PredMem raises unconditional sequence-structure co-generation success by 3.6, 17.7, and 48.7 percentage points, respectively, while improving the quality-diversity trade-off and suppressing repetitive mode collapse. Controlled diagnostics show that these gains stem primarily from early trajectory stabilization in unanchored cross-modal co-evolution rather than extra compute or simple entropy reduction, establishing PredMem as an efficient inference mechanism for multimodal discrete generation.

title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
authors: Weicong Zhang, Yuan Huang, Yu Zheng, Lin Chenxiao, Yingying Li, Lilong Fan, Liangdong Zhuang, Yufan Chen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiaming Zhang
abstract: Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP). To enable broader evaluation, we collect a new dataset, WHOLE, using a UAV platform across Weak-geometry, High-dynamic, Omnidirectional, Low-light, and Easy scenarios. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and WHOLE demonstrate competitive rendering quality and improved geometric accuracy relative to perspective systems. Compared with existing panoramic baselines, GOLD-SLAM improves mean PSNR by 5.56-9.10 dB and reduces mean Depth-L1 by 71.9-83.9%. To assess deployment feasibility on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs, we evaluate an embedded configuration of GOLD-SLAM on a Jetson Orin NX (16 GB), demonstrating online operation at the cost of reconstruction quality.

title: FlowVecFont: Scalable Vector Font Generation via Latent Flow Matching
authors: Takumu Fujioka, Gouhei Tanaka
abstract: Fonts are natively represented as vector outlines. Many existing studies on vector font generation have relied on specialized generation or refinement mechanisms, bitmap representations, or externally pretrained models to address the challenges of learning vector representations. These approaches often increase system complexity, incur additional computational and implementation costs, and introduce dependencies on external resources. We show that scaling a simple model enables high-quality pure vector font generation without external pretraining. We propose FlowVecFont, a scalable model for vector font generation based on latent flow matching and trained solely on vector outlines. A Transformer-based variational autoencoder maps glyph sequences into fixed-length continuous latent tokens, enabling standard conditional flow matching for vector glyph generation. The model supports conditioning on class labels or reference glyphs, with the latter enabling generalization to unseen characters and fonts. Experiments on 5M glyphs collected across Google Fonts, including non-Latin characters, show that generation quality improves with model scale across conditioning strategies. In a comparison on Latin glyphs, the 800M-parameter FlowVecFont outperforms DeepVecFont-v2 and DesigNet and achieves quality competitive with the pretrained 27B-parameter VecGlypher. We also provide TorchFont, a machine learning library for vector fonts.

title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
authors: Martín Escardó, Paulo Oliva
abstract: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. Finally, we formally establish the correctness of our construction by proving that the monadic alpha-beta search computes the same optimal outcomes and plays as exhaustive minimax search. Our results demonstrate how a foundational algorithm in AI can be expressed and verified using standard monadic abstractions, providing a basis for further development of compositional approaches to adversarial search.

title: Curvilinear nanomagnets of non-trivial geometric topology
authors: Vagson L. Carvalho-Santos, Luke A. Turnbull, Naëmi Leo, Oleksandr V. Pylypovskyi
abstract: In this Chapter, we focus on the question of how the global geometric characteristics given by the topology of the sample's shape are reflected in the properties of the magnetization field of the given curvilinear nanoarchitecture. We start with a brief introduction to differential geometry and topology, giving their connection to the specific properties of the vector field represented by the magnetization field defined at the specific manifold. Then we discuss modern fabrication and characterization techniques that make analysis of a sample's topology not only an interesting theoretical concept but also a directly accessible and practically relevant topic. The main attention of the Chapter is dedicated to the theoretical and experimental analysis of nanostructrures with the topology different from the extended films beyond the in-depth studied topic of tubes of the constant radius. In particular, toroidal, spherical, and non-orientable manifolds are considered.

title: Towards a Multimodal Aesthetic Agent for Photographic Reference Grading
authors: Kunjie Lin, Haitao Zhang, Bosheng Chen, Lanhui Xu, Gaofeng Pan, Yuxin Lin, Tianjiao Liu, Yi Yang, Yue Huang, Xinghao Ding, Zixu Lin, Yunlong Lin
abstract: Reference-guided photographic color grading helps users realize their aesthetic intent by selectively drawing on the color and tonal characteristics of a reference photograph. Doing so requires understanding which characteristics users wish to adopt and translating these preferences into controllable edits. However, image-only reference methods align overall appearance without instruction-grounded selection, while pixel-space generative editors typically produce flattened images without editable parameters, limiting subsequent refinement. To address these challenges, we introduce JarvisAura, a multimodal aesthetic agent that formulates photographic color grading as structured decision-making in an editable parameter space. JarvisAura offers three key advantages: (1) an aesthetic agent paradigm that integrates visual attribute perception, strategy-level reasoning, and parameterized execution for interpretable and controllable photographic color grading; (2) a unified reasoning-to-execution pipeline that connects aesthetic planning with backend rendering and editable parameter refinement; and (3) a three-stage training strategy comprising Parameter-Grounded Continual Pre-Training for parameter-appearance grounding, Reference-Grounded Supervised Fine-Tuning for reference-guided reasoning and parameter decisions, and Reference-Aligned Group Relative Policy Optimization for rendered-outcome refinement with multidimensional rewards and dynamic data derivation. On Ref-Bench, JarvisAura achieves the best scores among methods with results across reported automatic metrics and a 74% human-rated task-success rate, exceeding GPT-Image-2.5 by 9 percentage points.

title: DAiSy: Online Data Selection by Adaptive Utility Estimation for LLM Pretraining
authors: Simin Fan, Martin Jaggi
abstract: Model-aware online data selection prioritizes the training documents that contribute the most given the model's current state. Existing online selectors rank candidates upon gradient-based data utility scores, which requires the full forward-backward pass of the main model on every candidate document. Scoring each document therefore pays as much as training on it, yet only a small fraction is used for the real model update. We introduce DAiSy, a lightweight linear auxiliary model that learns to predict data utility scores from frozen document embeddings, which eliminates the computation overhead and infrastructure burdens. The linear estimator is updated alongside the main language model, fitting to the exact gradient-based utility scores obtained from the backward pass of regular training steps. Consequently, scoring a candidate requires only a linear transformation, bypassing the costly gradient-alignment computation. We demonstrate its effectiveness and efficiency for LLM pretraining in English and multilingual scenarios, with various steering target designs. The improvements from DAiSy can consistently survive the instruction-tuning phase.

title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
authors: Masahiro Hoshino, Shuichi Matsukiyo, Takanobu Amano
abstract: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

title: Reproducing the Speech Labels of Qwen3-Omni's Talker: Mimi in bf16, and a Last-Frame Pitfall
authors: Yuxuan Chen
abstract: Qwen3-Omni speaks through a Talker predicting 16 codebooks of a 12.5 Hz audio codec, but the encoder that made its training labels was not released, so new voices cannot be trained on matching labels. We identify this encoder from the released model's behavior. White-box regression shows that the codebook embeddings of the Talker, its multi-token predictor and the Code2Wav decoder match the first 16 codebooks of kyutai's Mimi layer by layer. A decoder-based test looks convincing but fails calibration: decoders trained on known labels cannot tell them apart. Teacher-forced Talker likelihoods, calibrated with 13 code language models trained on known labels, do tell implementations apart: the Talker prefers labels from kyutai's moshi package with bf16 weights over every other variant we tried. Loudness normalization and band-limiting of 20% or more of the data are ruled out. Separately, transformers' MimiModel encodes the last frame differently from kyutai's encoder unless the input length is a multiple of 1920 samples. After LoRA fine-tuning on its labels, 44--55% of generated sentences end in a noise burst, and the same frame costs the Mimi-based CSM-1B 119 nats; padding the input removes both. We release the encoding recipe, a label checker and a Talker fine-tuning toolkit.

title: Pando: Noise-Coupled Parallel Draft Trees for Efficient Edge Speculative Decoding
authors: Joren Dumoulin, Hyoukjun Kwon, Subhankar Pal, Steven Li, Vignesh Vivekraja, Marian Verhelst
abstract: Autoregressive (AR) decoding emits one token per forward pass, reloading the full model each time, so LLM inference on edge devices is memory-bound while the compute units sit idle. Speculative decoding puts that idle compute to work by verifying several drafted tokens in a single pass. State-of-the-art parallel drafters such as DFlash and DSpark propose an entire block of draft tokens in one forward pass, which makes drafting compute-efficient. However, they are deployed with draft chains whose length is capped by the block size they are trained for, leaving most of the computational budget for verification unused. To tackle this problem, we propose Pando, which builds dynamic draft trees on top of a parallel drafter and thereby removes this cap. Pando employs noise-coupled pruning, which draws the target model's sampling noise before drafting and ranks candidate branches under that noise, so the tree retains the branches the target will actually sample. Noise coupling is lossless and requires no retraining or additional model pass, yet increases acceptance length by up to $8.4\%$ on Qwen3-8B. To optimize and evaluate Pando configurations across hardware, we normalize an operator-level roofline to AR decoding, reducing every platform to its ridge point. On a representative edge device, a 16-node Pando tree attains $5.3\times$ speedup and $4.2\times$ energy reduction over AR decoding: $25\%$ faster than DSpark's released chain, and $27\%$ faster and $72\%$ more energy-efficient than an EAGLE-3 tree. The best configurations remain memory-bound on every edge device we model, so added compute capacity does not reduce their latency.

title: RoboDemo: Reconciling Demonstration Intent and Execution Progress for Long-Horizon Manipulation
authors: Xiangkai Ma, Zhihao Yuan, Linbo Zhai, Xinyi Wang, Junjie Wang, Sheng Xu, Guiliang Liu, Han Zhang, Chuyi Chen, Jifeng Gao, Wenzhong Li
abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires more than predicting the next action from the current observation. The policy must maintain a global procedural prior that specifies the expected progress of each subtask stage, while also tracking the realized progress produced by its interactions. To this end, we propose RoboDemo, a demonstration-augmented manipulation framework built on Dual-Cascaded Test-Time-Training. RoboDemo accepts either a task-relevant human demonstration video or a semantically compatible robot video retrieved from simulation corpus as reference, allowing us to evaluate its applicability with and without paired human demonstrations. Task semantics and physical motion information from the reference video are then transferred into persistent demonstration-intent memory. During deployment, we causally compress online observations, robot states, and executed actions into interaction-progress memory. To keep reference intent stable while interaction progress continually evolves, reference and execution video tokens independently update their respective fast-weight states. The action expert performs cascaded memory reads, first obtaining reference guidance and then refining it using realized progress, allowing the policy to adapt to execution deviations without overwriting the stored intent. RoboDemo achieves 90.7% success on Imitator Game and 73.3% success across three real-world household tasks. Real-world videos, code and hf-weights are available in our project website.

title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
authors: Shengyong Pan
abstract: We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees. For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings. Further applications concern connected outer automorphism group schemes over perfect fields, the kernels of the quotient maps on ordinary algebraic $K$-theory, and the nonconnective $K$-theory of enhanced relative singularity categories. We construct biadjoint representatives over Henselian Noetherian local rings and relative stable tensor functors for almost $ν$-stable derived equivalences. We also answer a question of Abe and Hoshino about preservation of the Gorenstein condition in a fixed codimension.

title: Can You Find the Edit When Nothing Looks Wrong? A Paired Benchmark for Text-Driven Image Manipulation Localization Beyond Semantic Abnormality
authors: Peiyu Zhuang, Jianquan Yang, Zhuoying Cai, Yi Jiang, Yingquan Chen, Xinle Wang, Zeqin Yu, Dongdong Lin, Ruitao Xie, Kaige Li, Xiaochun Cao
abstract: Instruction-driven image editing can alter a photograph while keeping the result coherent with the scene. Existing benchmarks lack matched plausible and anomalous edits of the same target, making it difficult to measure how localization performance changes with semantic plausibility. We construct a paired benchmark by generating semantically plausible and anomalous replacements of the same target in each source photograph. Both edits use the same editor, language, and generation settings. We estimate a separate mask for each output and retain pairs with sufficient mask overlap, enabling direct comparison of localization performance under the two semantic conditions. The release contains 47,747 bilingual triplets from 6,500 photographs, spanning four editors, three source domains, and six intended violation types. Across nine public localizers, editor-averaged IoU is lower on plausible edits in 26 of 27 model-dataset comparisons. This gap persists under pixel-change controls and region-size analyses. These findings reveal a semantic-plausibility shortcut: localization often weakens when an edited result looks ordinary. The benchmark provides a controlled setting for measuring this gap and developing localizers that remain effective on plausible edits.

title: ST-SfM: Spatio-Temporal Structure-from-Motion for Initialising 4D Gaussian Splatting
authors: Harshit, Sami Brandt
abstract: Dynamic Gaussian splatting is usually initialised either with random points or with a structure-from-motion (SfM) cloud of the first frame. Neither says anything about what moves, where and when. We introduce ST-SfM, a sparse spatio-temporal SfM for synchronised, calibrated multi-camera video that splits the scene into two branches. Static structure is detected once per camera on a temporal-median image, gated for temporal stability and matched along epi-polar lines. Motion is detected as space-time interest points (STIPs) in the video volume, described with HOG3D and matched only between candidates that agree both epipolarly and in time. Union-find tracks that refuse inconsistent merges are triangulated with RANSAC over all view pairs, giving static 3D points and dynamic 4D points (x, y, z, t) with sub-frame times. We use ST-SfM derived sparse 4D cloud to initialise 4D Gaussian splatting. In comparison with random initialisation on N3DV scenes we get improvements in PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS.

title: Relational Bottleneck Models
authors: Shin'ya Yamaguchi, Kosuke Nishida
abstract: Achieving both interpretable and high-performance inference is a key challenge in deep learning. While Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) provide inherent interpretability, they are constrained by task-specific training and rely on isolated visual concepts that fail to capture higher-order visual semantic relationships. Conversely, Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate zero-shot capabilities through Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. However, standard CoT lacks a strict causal dependency between the generated rationale and the final output, compromising faithfulness. To bridge this gap, we propose Relational Bottleneck Models (RBMs), a novel training-free framework that transforms any off-the-shelf LVLMs into inherently interpretable models in a plug-and-play manner. RBMs consist of two stages: (i) Structured Rationale Generation (SRG), which explicitly models semantic interactions between visual concepts as subject-predicate-object triplets, and (ii) Rationale-Grounded Decoding (RGD), which enforces a strict causal dependency between the rationales and the final output. RGD aggregates rationale-conditional next-token distributions via an importance-weighted product-of-experts strategy, strictly excluding the image inputs from the decoding context. Extensive zero-shot evaluations across diverse benchmarks and LVLM backbones demonstrate that RBMs achieve superior interpretability while improving task performance over CBM baselines, entirely without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Relation Before Action: Explicit Relation Modeling for Latent Action Pretraining
authors: Boning Zhang, Junyu Gao, Changsheng Xu
abstract: Learning latent actions from unlabeled video sequences offers a promising way to acquire reusable action representations without relying on embodiment-specific control annotations. However, existing latent-action pretraining approaches commonly couple the modeling of visual transitions with action inference, directly mapping paired observations or derived transition cues into latent action codes. This formulation leaves two distinct tasks entangled: characterizing the relational structure of an observed transition and abstracting it into a compact action representation. We propose RELACT, a relation-first framework that explicitly separates transition relation modeling from predictive action abstraction. RELACT first constructs a structured relation representation $R$ that captures how visual elements and their interactions evolve across observations. It then infers a compact, state-conditioned stochastic latent action $U$, whose predictive effects are learned through action-conditioned latent dynamics. The resulting action representation can be grounded in native control spaces for model-based planning or used to supervise downstream embodied policies. Extensive experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain image-goal navigation, goal-conditioned manipulation, and downstream policy adaptation demonstrate improved predictive action representations and consistent gains in planning and control, supporting the effectiveness and generality of relation-first latent action pretraining.

title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
authors: Zhi-Rong Deng, Jie Yang
abstract: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.

title: Observable sets for one-dimensional Schrödinger equations with subquadratic power potentials
authors: Yanchuan Wang
abstract: In this paper, we study observability inequalities for the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation associated with the operator $H_m=-\partial_x^2+|x|^{2m}$, where $0<m\leq1$. For $0<m<1/2$, observability in some positive time, and equivalently in every positive time, is characterized by the thickness of the observation set. This extends the characterization of Chen--Liu--Liu at $m=1/2$. For $1/2<m\leq1$, we characterize observable sets in terms of the asymptotic lower density on the spatial intervals $I_{m,a}(x)=[x-a|x|^{2m-1},x+a|x|^{2m-1}]$. Observability in some positive time is equivalent to positive density at some scale, whereas observability in every positive time is equivalent to positive density at every scale. Moreover, for $1/2<m<1$, the minimal observation time is comparable to the square root of the critical density scale.

title: EvoSearch: Self-Evolving Active Perception for Wide-Area Geospatial Search
authors: Zhenghao Xie, Jing Xiao, Zihao Yu, Wanyi Yu, Liang Liao, Gui-Song Xia, Mi Wang
abstract: Geospatial search is fundamental to resource surveys and environmental monitoring, requiring the discovery of relevant evidence across large geographic areas and multiple spatial scales. Existing active perception methods adaptively select observation locations and scales to improve search efficiency, yet their search trajectories become increasingly long and costly as the search area expands. A key limitation is that final-answer correctness alone provides little guidance on which observations to retain and when to stop, hindering efficient wide-area search. To address this challenge, we propose EvoSearch, a self-evolving active perception framework that co-evolves the perception policy and exploration program to compress search trajectories while preserving answer quality. Specifically, quality-cost comparisons between completed branches from shared evidence train the policy to acquire useful observations, avoid redundant ones, and stop when sufficient evidence is available. Execution feedback from the updated policy then guides exploration-program revision, adapting experience generation to the policy's changing observation needs. We further introduce GeoSearchBench, a benchmark for evaluating search quality and visual processing efficiency through relational search and region search. Experiments demonstrate that EvoSearch shortens search trajectories and substantially reduces visual processing while maintaining overall search quality, supporting scalable active perception for wide-area geospatial search.

title: The polarization bundle of a bending ray: nested projections and helicity Chern numbers
authors: Didier Felbacq, Emmanuel Rousseau
abstract: We consider a ray propagating in a weakly anisotropic, possibly absorbing medium. The transverse planes of the propagation directions form a rank-two complex vector bundle $E_\perp$ over the sphere $S^2$ of directions. The polarization states are the points of $Z=\mathbb{CP}(E_\perp)$. Projecting the flat derivative of $\mathbb{C}^3$ onto $E_\perp$ gives a connection $D$, the complexified Levi-Civita connection of $S^2$, whose holonomy is the Rytov rotation. Projecting $D$ onto a polarization line gives the connection of the tautological line bundle over $Z$, whose holonomy is the Pancharatnam--Berry phase. For the horizontal distribution defined by $D$, the curvature of this bundle is $iω_{\mathrm{FS}}$ on the vertical part, $i s_3\,ω$ on the horizontal part, and zero on the mixed part. Here $ω_{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the Fubini--Study form, $ω$ the area form of $S^2$, and $s_3$ the circular Stokes parameter. The Rytov rotation, the Pancharatnam--Berry phase and the Chern numbers $c_1(L_\pm)=\mp 2$ are all obtained from this curvature. Restricted to the helicity sections, it gives the obstruction to a globally smooth circular Jones vector, although the circular polarization states are globally defined.

title: Parity-check matrices and their MDS or NMDS properties for several classes of non-GRS type linear codes
authors: Zhonghao Liang, Chenlu Jia, Qunying Liao
abstract: Parity-check matrices and weight distributions are important for understanding the structure and performance of linear codes. However, obtaining explicit expressions for them is often challenging. In recent years, numerous families of non-GRS type linear codes have been constructed, motivated by applications in coding theory and cryptography. For many of these codes, explicit parity-check matrices remain unavailable, hindering further investigation of their duality properties, decoding methods, and weight distributions. In this paper, we first develop a method for constructing parity-check matrices using code extensions and Cramer's rule, and then apply this method or through direct constructions to obtain explicit parity-check matrices for column-twisted generalized Reed--Solomon codes (TGRS), modified GRS codes and so on. Second, we introduce the $(Ł,¶)$-twisted generalized Roth--Lempel (TGRL) code $\C_{k,\ell}(Ł,¶,\A_{m\times m},\B)$, obtain explicit parity-check matrices for three subclasses through direct constructions, and establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $\C_{k,\ell}(Ł,¶,\A_{2\times 2},\B)$ with the most general $Ł$, $¶$, and $\B$ to be maximum distance separable (MDS). For one-column TGRS codes, we prove that they are either MDS or near MDS (NMDS), furthermore, establish a necessary and sufficient condition for them to be NMDS, and determine the weight distribution of a family of these NMDS codes using subset sums in finite abelian groups. Finally, basing on known results for non-GRS properties of TGRS codes, we establish sufficient conditions for these codes considered in this paper to be non-GRS from the perspective of punctured codes.

title: FlashSegmentator: High-Throughput TotalSegmentator Inference without Loss of Accuracy
authors: Yosuke Yamagishi, Tomohiro Kikuchi, Shouhei Hanaoka, Takeharu Yoshikawa, Osamu Abe
abstract: Purpose: To develop, evaluate, and publicly release FlashSegmentator, an open-source inference pipeline that increases the throughput of TotalSegmentator without retraining or loss of segmentation accuracy. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study used public datasets: 73 CT examinations from the TotalSegmentator test split (median age, 65 years; 37 male, 35 female, one unknown), 30 abdominal CT examinations from the Beyond the Cranial Vault (BTCV) dataset, 512 training-split CT examinations for concurrent-process analysis, and 55 MRI examinations. FlashSegmentator adds static-shape compilation, pipelining, batched sliding-window inference, and GPU postprocessing. Throughput was compared with the reference implementation (including its lower-resolution modes) and FastSegmentator on GH200, A100, and T4 GPUs. Dice agreement was tested with two one-sided tests (margin, +/-0.01). Results: FlashSegmentator processed 3782, 1810, and 270 examinations per hour on the GH200, A100, and T4 (57.7, 33.9, and 6.4 times the reference implementation and 3.20, 2.50, and 1.22 times compiled FastSegmentator). Dice scores were equivalent for all 117 structures on every GPU (mean difference <= 1.2 x 10^-5; P < .001) and at the examination level on BTCV. In contrast, the lower-resolution modes of the reference implementation processed 181 and 213 examinations per hour on the A100 but reduced mean Dice by 0.116 and 0.241. On MRI, throughput increased 94-fold with all 50 structures equivalent. Estimated A100 cloud cost per 10,000 examinations decreased from 997 to 29 US dollars. Conclusion: FlashSegmentator increased the throughput of TotalSegmentator on data center and entry-level GPUs without loss of segmentation accuracy compared with the reference implementation.

title: Some conservativity results for weak arithmetic theories in a language with exponentiation
authors: Konstantin Kovalyov
abstract: Recall that $\mathsf{IOpen}$ denotes the theory of quantifier-free induction in the pure arithmetic language. In this paper, we consider an extension of $\mathsf{IOpen}$ in the arithmetical language expanded by the unary function $\exp: x \mapsto 2^x$, obtained by adding certain simple universal axioms for $\exp$, namely, $$\exp(1) = 2, \quad \exp(x + y) = \exp(x) \exp(y), \quad \exp(x) > x.$$ We prove that this theory is $Π_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{IOpen}$ and $\forall$-conservative over the theory of discretely ordered $\mathbb Z$-semirings. This result extends a result of A. Wilkie and provides a partial answer to a question of E. Jeřábek concerning the strength of the theory of exponential integer parts.

title: The backtrackless circuits of $D(k,q)$ obtained by lifting
authors: Xiaoyan Cheng, Chen Zhang, Yuansheng Tang, Ming Xu
abstract: For integer $k\geq2$ and power $q$ of prime $p$, the algebraic bipartite graph $D(k,q)$, proposed by Lazebnik and Ustimenko in 1993, is $q$-regular, edge-transitive and of girth at least $k+4$.
