Dynamic-window analyses show that GRAFT restores local dynamics while preserving the stable backbone structure. These results suggest a new principle for high-utility forecasting: predict the backbone, then graft the dynamics.

title: DexOPD: Dual-Extrapolation On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models
authors: Yunchao Ke, Yanzhe Hu, Yi Yang, Jiachun Jin, Zhihong Liu, Zhijie Deng
abstract: Flow-based diffusion models have become a mainstream paradigm for text-to-image generation, where task-specific post-training produces specialist models with complementary strengths. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (OPD) offers an efficient way to consolidate these specialists into a single unified student. Recent methods strengthen supervision through teacher extrapolation, constructing stronger proxy teachers that allow distilled students to surpass the original specialists. However, their extrapolation directions remain defined solely by frozen teacher and reference models, leaving the student's own training progress unexploited. To address this limitation, we introduce DexOPD, a dual-extrapolation on-policy distillation method for diffusion models. DexOPD retains extrapolated teacher supervision while leveraging a lagging historical student as the reference for student self-extrapolation. Sampling across multiple self-extrapolation gains from shared initial noise broadens exploration along the student's evolving trajectory, and task rewards convert pairwise differences in candidate quality into a normalized auxiliary regression direction. Empirically, we evaluate DexOPD on GenEval, OCR, and DrawBench. The resulting unified SD3.5-Medium student achieves a GenEval reward of 0.9736, an OCR score of 0.9515, and a DrawBench Aesthetic score of 6.4875, surpassing the corresponding specialist teachers as well as all evaluated OPD and multi-task reinforcement learning baselines across these three benchmarks while preserving standard single-model inference.

title: Audits Need Access, Data, and Compute. But How Much?
authors: Salil Goyal, Sarah H. Cen, Daniel E. Ho
abstract: AI audits have garnered significant attention in recent months, as the ability to test and monitor AI models plays a crucial role in safe development and deployment. However, AI audit success hinges on an auditor's authority; in particular, what information and resources they have at their disposal. Ongoing debates have surrounded the question: How much model access is needed to conduct an AI audit? Auditors seek more model access, while companies resist it for reasons related to confidential business information (trade secrets) and privacy. This tug-of-war remains unresolved. Further, this debate misses a related question: How much data and compute do auditors need? In this work, we systematically investigate both questions. We provide a framework that varies each of these three dimensions-model access, data, and compute-and measures their joint effect on audit success. We apply this framework to three tasks. We find that (1) some model access is important, but there can be diminishing returns; (2) data and compute matter more for traditional fairness audits, but model access matters more for manipulation and lie detection; and (3) these three resources can be fungible (i.e., an exchange rate exists between them), meaning that model access is not the only salient factor. These results suggest that audit governance should jointly consider different dimensions of auditor authority (including model access, data, and compute) in relation to audit objectives. These issues are particularly salient as we consider the spectrum of auditing setups, from a small ecosystem of embedded evaluators with significant access to a large body of third-party auditors with greater independence but limited access. Our framework serves as a template that can be applied to different audit tasks and inform the degree of auditor authority.

title: Sounding the Black Box: Online Training of Embedded Neural Networks in Forward-Only Physical Simulators
authors: Ruiqi Shu, Tianrun Gao, Haomin Wen, Xiaomeng Huang
abstract: Hybrid physics-neural simulators embed neural networks in partial differential equation (PDE) solvers to model unresolved subgrid dynamics while preserving resolved physics and conservation laws. Because closure outputs feed back across time steps, single-step offline regression does not directly minimize multi-step rollout error, motivating online trajectory optimization. Solver backpropagation through time (BPTT) is the standard online solution when solver derivatives are available, yet many operational Fortran and C/C++ simulators expose only non-differentiable, forward-only interfaces. We introduce FORGE (Forward-Only Response and Gauss-Newton Estimation), an online framework that trains embedded networks from forward runs alone by decoupling exact network derivatives from black-box simulator dynamics. Stage I warms up the rollout via a low-dimensional Gauss-Newton step along output-orthonormal weight directions, canceling multi-layer feature drift via a final-layer correction. Stage II perturbs spatial output fields to fit a gain-bounded causal linear response operator across rollout steps, solves for regularized target outputs, and updates all weights via network backpropagation. Across five 2D and 3D benchmarks spanning phase separation, reaction-diffusion, fluid and MHD turbulence, and ocean circulation, FORGE outperforms gradient-free, reinforcement-learning, and emulator-based baselines, cutting coarse-solver test mean squared error (MSE) by 50%-96% in 2D and 70% in 3D, outperforming the strongest forward-only baseline by 16%-69%, and recovering 88%-98% of Solver BPTT's gains. Code is available at https://github.com/ChiyodaMomo01/FORGE.

title: Typical-query energy figures mislead institutional AI electricity demand
authors: Nathan Garland, Ryan Heneghan
abstract: Institutions increasingly buy large language model services, yet we still often estimate electricity use as single Wh-per-query value. We present the Surrogate Large Language Energy Emulator (SULLEE), an open bottom-up model linking token geometry, serving hardware, and workflow structure to annual institutional electricity, with uncertainty propagated by Monte Carlo simulation. When an institution multiplies a single reported "typical" per-query energy figure by its count of visible user prompts our modelling implies that this compounds two separable shortfalls: a right-skewed task-energy distribution not represented by any single scalar, and workflow amplification of each visible prompt into additional agent and tool calls. Together these imply an underestimate of total inference electricity by a factor of approximately 3.4 under present-day observed use, rising to approximately 15 under a 2030 high-integration scenario. Using Australian public universities as a case study, we show how the top 10% of highest-energy requests contributes over half of modelled institution-level energy use. We quantify how institution-level electricity demand may increase across three AI integration scenarios of: 1) a continuation of estimated present-day 2026 usage; 2) a high-uptake present-day 2026 institution, and 3) a potential 2030 uptake scenario - based on present trends of generative AI tools and their uptake. For a representative Australian university, mean annual electricity demand for AI inference purposes is projected to increase from 17.3 MWh (with a 3.1-47.1 MWh uncertainty, within P05-P95 scenario quartile ranges) under the 2026 observed-use scenario to up to 287.4 MWh (41.5-830.7 MWh) by 2030.

title: Antiferroelectric Fluids with Hierarchical Polar Organization
authors: Hiroya Nishikawa, Hina Saito, Tetsu Katayama, Atsuko Nihonyanagi, Dennis Kwaria, Hiroyuki Inuzuka, Junxi Liu, Go Watanabe, Fumito Araoka
abstract: The discovery of the ferroelectric nematic (NF) phase has accelerated research on fluids exhibiting polar order along the molecular long axis. However, their antiferroelectric (AFE) counterparts remain less explored. Here, we investigate how terminal alkyl-chain elongation competes with polar core-core interactions in a homologous series. This series exhibits modulated AFE order accompanied by SmC-type cybotactic correlations, with the AFE phase persisting in homologs bearing terminal alkyl chains of up to 17 carbon atoms. Three distinct phase sequences on cooling lead to two types of two-dimensional (2D) AFE lattices. Multiple sharp X-ray diffraction (XRD) peaks reveal rectangular and oblique lattice structures, supporting their classification as AFE columnar phases. XRD analysis and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support a hierarchical structural model in which locally aligned polar molecules occupy thin segments of finite width within polar columns. The columns occupy the sites of a 2D lattice, with neighboring columns polarized in opposite directions. This model provides a structural framework for understanding the distinct precursor phase sequences and links packing between columns to the resulting AFE superstructures.

title: VLG-Drive: Unifying Vision-Language and Geometric Priors for Autonomous Driving
authors: Junge Zhang, Jie Zhu, Yanqi Jia, Xiangyu Xu, Zixun Huang, Wenbin He, Xin Li, Jiachen Li, Liu Ren
abstract: A driving planner needs both scene semantics, which vision-language models (VLMs) provide, and spatial structure, which geometric foundation models recover from visual history. We present VLG-Drive, which keeps both models frozen and trains only a fusion interface and a planner from trajectory labels. At each camera-grid cell, the interface fuses the paired VLM and geometry features into one joint token through a geometry-anchored residual, and a command-conditioned planner reads these tokens to predict the ego trajectory. VLG-Drive achieves 31.78 EPDMS on NavHard under perturbed initial states, the highest among the compared methods, and 88.27 PDMS on NavTest from cameras alone. Pointwise fusion outperforms independent VLM and geometry streams on both benchmarks. In closed-loop driving on 420 HUGSIM scenarios, VLG-Drive outperforms all compared planners. These results indicate that a lightweight planner trained on fused features of frozen vision-language and geometric foundation models is an effective alternative to adapting either model for planning.

title: DraftKV: Protecting Persistent Worlds through Hierarchical Streaming Retrieval
authors: Xiaoling Zhou, Haopeng Li, Yufa Zhou, Rui Ding, Yu Li, Jun Lin, Enze Xie, Chunhua Shen, Xuan Shen
abstract: Interactive video world models enable action- and camera-controlled exploration, yet struggle to maintain consistent spatial geometry and appearance when revisiting previously explored locations. Historical KV caches help auto-regressive video diffusion models maintain long-term consistency, but their retrieval and attention computation introduce substantial latency as history grows. We propose DraftKV, a training-free framework that retrieves historical KV caches based on geometric grounding and query-conditioned relevance, while combining CPU offloading with tile-wise streaming attention to reduce GPU memory usage and inference latency. Theoretically, we show that draft relevance reproduces the mean branch of full-resolution block relevance exactly, so its deviation is confined to the $β$-weighted max branch, and we bound retrieval utility loss in terms of the measured Top-K selection overlap. We further show that draft relevance cannot distinguish blocks with similar pooled descriptors regardless of camera pose, motivating geometric grounding before refinement. Then, we introduce streaming CG-Attention, which overlaps CPU-to-GPU KV transfers with attention computation through tile-wise streaming, hiding transfer latency while maintaining bounded GPU memory usage. Experiments across diverse model families show that DraftKV achieves superior generation quality and consistency while achieving $3.27\times$ end-to-end speedup and 42.2% peak GPU memory reduction over other CPU-offloaded KV cache retrieval methods. Notably, DraftKV enables high-quality interactive world generation with historical KV retrieval on a single H100 GPU using SolarWM-33B.

title: Global full-f gyrokinetic analysis of energetic-particle-driven Alfvén eigenmodes and their phase-space drive with GYSELA
authors: S. Raj, Y. W. Cho, Z. S. Qu, G. Brochard, L. Bramucci, P. Donnel, R. Bigué, M. Go, S. Mazzi, G. Dif-Pradalier, D. Zarzoso, K. Obrejan, V. Grandgirard, Y. Sarazin, K. Lim, X. Garbet
abstract: We investigate the linear stability of energetic-particle (EP) driven Alfvén eigenmodes and the wave-particle interaction in phase space, using the newly implemented energetic-particle module in the electromagnetic global full-f gyrokinetic code GYSELA. The coupled gyrokinetic-Maxwell system self-consistently evolves the EP species alongside thermal ions and kinetic electrons, retaining finite-orbit-width and global profile effects. To mitigate the relaxation of the initial distribution in global full-f models, a canonical Maxwellian initialisation is employed, which strongly reduces this relaxation and the associated change of the drive. The framework is verified against the ITPA-TAE and the reversed-shear NLED-AUG cases, including scans in EP temperature and density. The agreement with published multi-code results is quantitative for the ITPA-TAE case and qualitative for the NLED-AUG case, where a reversed-shear Alfvén eigenmode (RSAE) is found near $q_{\rm min}$. Beyond verification, we use a constants-of-motion (CoM) diagnostic to project the gyrocentre distribution and the local wave-particle power exchange ($P = -\mathbf{J}\cdot\mathbf{E}$) onto invariant space. This identifies the orbit classes and resonances that interact with the mode. For the ITPA-TAE, deeply co-passing orbits dominate the drive. For the NLED-AUG RSAE, counter-passing orbits drive the mode and co-passing orbits damp it, and the sign of the exchange follows that of the linear EP drive. These results provide a basis for future global full-f studies of nonlinear energetic-particle transport and mode saturation.

title: The Eclipsing $γ$ Doradus Star VZ Canum Venaticorum
authors: Jae Woo Lee
abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the eclipsing binary VZ CVn using TESS Sectors 50 and 77 photometry together with published spectroscopic results. The TESS light curves were modeled to refine the binary parameters, and the residual light curves were analyzed to investigate the pulsational properties of the system. We derive masses and radii of $M_{\rm A}=1.526\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm A}=1.638\pm0.023$ $R_\odot$ for the primary and $M_{\rm B}=1.259\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm B}=1.133\pm0.016$ $R_\odot$ for the secondary. Comparison with PARSEC evolutionary models suggests a near-solar metallicity of $Z=0.017$ and an age of 1.0 Gyr. Separate frequency analyses of the two TESS sectors reveal four signals with possible counterparts in both sectors. Two of these frequencies, $f_2=4.7486$ day$^{-1}$ and $f_6=7.1242$ day$^{-1}$, are consistent with the fourth and sixth orbital harmonics, respectively, suggesting an orbital origin rather than independent $δ$ Sct pulsations. The dominant frequency $f_1=1.7577$ day$^{-1}$ has a pulsation constant of $Q_1=0.336$ day, consistent with a $γ$ Dor-type g-mode pulsation. The weaker signal $f_5=1.9754$ day$^{-1}$ also has a pulsation constant of $Q_5=0.299$ day, although its detection remains tentative because of its low S/N. Together with the physical and evolutionary properties of the primary, these results support its classification as a $γ$ Dor pulsator rather than the previously proposed $γ$ Dor--$δ$ Sct hybrid pulsator.

title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
authors: Zhen Wu, De-xuan Xu
abstract: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $ε$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

title: On SQG Patches with $H^2$ Regularity
authors: Shaoqing Chen, Yongzhong Sun
abstract: In this paper, we study patch solutions of the generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations, which is an interpolation between the 2D Euler ($β=0$) and the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equations ($β=1$). We establish in the SQG case, the local well-posedness for patches with $H^2$ boundaries, which improves the previous result of $H^{2+s}$, $s>0$ by Gancedo--Nguyen--Patel \cite{Gancedo2022}. Also, in the gSQG case with $0<β<1$, the uniqueness of $H^2$ patch solutions is established. Our proofs are based on the contour dynamics formulation with constant speed, introduced in \cite{Gancedo2008}.

title: Eisenstein Cohomology and Critical Values of Certain \(L\)-Functions: A Root-Theoretic Combinatorial Lemma
authors: Farid Hosseinijafari
abstract: This paper gives a root-theoretic extension of the Harder--Raghuram combinatorial lemma, relating criticality of adjacent $L-$values to degrees in nilradical cohomology, to maximal parabolics $P=MU$ of connected split reductive groups with irreducible, essentially tempered cohomological inducing data. At real places, the paper classifies the maximal parabolics for which the two Kostant degrees in the boundary comparison can agree at a regular shift. For each such parabolic, an admissible shift makes both adjacent arguments critical in every Langlands--Shahidi grade exactly when both Kostant degrees equal $\dim U/2$. The classification recovers the two-block parabolics of type $A$ with even product of block sizes (Harder--Raghuram, proved by Weselmann) and the isotropic-line parabolic of type $D_{2m+1}$ for $m\ge2$ (Bhagwat--Raghuram). The only exceptional cases are $P_1$ and $P_6$ of type $E_6$. In all other cases, roots of $U$ fixed by the longest Levi Weyl element confine simultaneous criticality to a singular wall, generalizing the odd-block obstruction for $\mathrm{GL}_N$. Their number is the difference of the fundamental ranks of $M$ and $G$. When the Kostant degrees differ, as in Harder's $\mathrm{GL}_2$ setting, the paper determines which boundary degrees can still coincide. At a complex place, an admissible shift is simultaneously critical exactly when the two conjugate Levi weights after the shift occur in Kostant degrees summing to $\dim U$. With a common relative center, total degree balance at a regular admissible shift characterizes simultaneous criticality at every archimedean place. For split $E_6$ over $\mathbb Q$, a half-spin family yields Eisenstein cohomology classes in degrees $20$ and $21$, including a degree-$20$ class with nonzero restrictions to both associate boundary face types.

title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
authors: Bo Liang, Minghui Du, Zhenwei Lyu, Hanlin Song, Jiakai Zhang, Weichen Qin, Chia-Jui Chou, Yi Yang, Jingyi Yu, Ziren Luo, Mingming Sun, Peng Xu, Yue-Liang Wu
abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

title: Linearization for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth
authors: Xiao Tang, Jiangqiong Yu
abstract: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound. We obtain representations of the displacement in terms of stable and unstable orbit series that converge uniformly on any bounded set and give the inverse conjugacy by using the Banach fixed points theorem in a weighted function space.

title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
authors: Ruixiao Shi, Fu Feng, Yucheng Xie, Jing Wang, Xin Geng
abstract: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed to assess emerging hypotheses. Their spatial attention guides view placement, contextual responses determine crop extent, and observation history encourages complementary inspection. The resulting predictions are combined through uncertainty-weighted voting. On ScreenSpot-Pro, SPARK improves grounding accuracy over single-view inference by 13.9, 25.2, and 16.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and UI-TARS, outperforming all compared test-time methods for each backbone. Consistent gains across four additional benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse interfaces and grounding tasks. These results establish semantic probing as an effective mechanism for turning a frozen VLM's understanding of what to inspect into more accurate GUI grounding.

title: A General Framework for E-process Stopping Rules in Best-Arm Identification
authors: Donghyun Park, Seohwa Hwang, Junyong Park
abstract: We propose an e-process stopping rule in the best-arm identification problem. The e-process stopping rule is different from the Chernoff stopping rule by its hypothesis structure on the stopping decision. The major benefit of an e-process stopping rule is the flexibility in stopping rule design and in fact, it recovers previously suggested Chernoff stopping rule on several bandit problems. Moreover, we analyze the asymptotic optimality of the $δ$-PAC algorithm with the decomposition of e-processes. The decomposition separates optimality conditions into three parts; the sampling policy allocation convergence, the efficiency of e-process design, and the bandit problem's inherent stochastic behavior. Subsequently, we prove a sufficient condition for asymptotic optimality in bandit algorithms. For the application of an e-process stopping rule, we derived an asymptotically optimal algorithm for the generalized linear bandit problem.

title: Moiré-Induced Interlayer Electron-Phonon Coupling in Graphene/hBN Superlattices
authors: Dasol Kim, Zhengguang Lu, Tonghang Han, Guorui Chen, Tianyi Han, Jixiang Yang, Bing Cheng, Zhenxian Liu, Christopher Homes, G. L. Carr, Jeong Min Park, Qihang Zhang, Lili Jiang, Hongyuan Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Feng Wang, Long Ju
abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moiré superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moiré potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moiré electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moiré superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moiré flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moiré electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.

title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
authors: Zheng Sun, Zhuo Li, Zhihao Li, Hengyi Sim, Ge Wang, Ziyue Zhu, Mingkai Jia, Fei Chen
abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents can iteratively self-improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, yet real-world tasks provide neither ground-truth success scorers nor resettable practice environments. Our key observation is that a single real demonstration simultaneously specifies scene geometry, defines the terminal success criterion, and serves as a physical reference trajectory for verifying world fidelity---all decoupled from the source robot's kinematics. We present {RESET}: we reconstruct a contact-rich world and derive a frozen read-only criterion from one demonstration ({R}ebuild); check that world against the demonstration by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency ({E}xamine); evolve modular white-box task graphs and skill code from per-node failure evidence ({S}elf-improve); deploy frozen code on real robots with zero runtime LLM calls ({E}xecute); and share the verified world and criterion with unseen robots without new demonstrations ({T}ransfer). On 8 manipulation tasks, each rebuilt from one real demonstration, RESET achieves 97% average success on unseen layouts in simulation, whereas zero-shot code reaches 27%, per-task fine-tuned pi0.5 policies 31%, and Diffusion Policy 50%; injecting reconstruction defects shows that practice tolerates many reconstruction errors, that geometric errors can still stall or mislead it, and that the check flags most of them while physical randomization covers the rest. Without any target demonstrations, 3 heterogeneous robots acquire the same task skills in the shared world: a robot with similar arms copies 95% of its skill functions unchanged from the source robot, while robots with different arms and hands write their own. In real-robot experiments, the resulting programs run on 4 robots and succeed in 80% of 280 trials.

title: Toward Database-Native Genomics: A Vision for Declarative Genomic Analysis
authors: Dhruv Aron, Danial Saleem, James Christopher Sorenson, Xiangyao Yu
abstract: In recent years, numerous advancements in relational database management systems (RDBMS), including cloud-native and GPU-native paradigms, have resulted in highly competitive RDBMS performance for analytical workloads. At the same time, the field of genomics has evolved into a data-intensive domain owing to the advent of next-generation sequencing; however, current genomic analysis workflows are often file-based, fragmented, and reliant on disparate tools, limiting their expressiveness, usability, performance, and scalability. This work argues for an incremental adoption of RDBMS and declarative SQL querying in genomic analysis, particularly tertiary analysis. By translating common tasks from widely-used tools like SAMtools and BEDtools into SQL queries executed in DuckDB, we demonstrate that off-the-shelf RDBMS can match or exceed the performance of existing tools while offering significant improvements in expressiveness and usability. We identify current limitations and propose practical paths forward, aiming to position relational databases as a foundational platform for modern bioinformatics workflows.

title: Cheap Memory Costs Future Compute: Co-Designing Persistent KV and GPU Execution for Efficient Streaming Video Diffusion
authors: Jian Yang, Zhizhuo Kou, Qiyuan Zhu, Han Chen, Sirui Han, Yike Guo
abstract: Block-causal video diffusion generates long videos block by block, conditioned on a persistent key-value (KV) cache. After each block is denoised, an extra noise-free ($t=0$) forward pass writes its clean KV into the cache; once distillation and speculative early exit make denoising cheap, this clean KV update dominates the runtime. Reusing stale KV shortens the update, but stale memory corrupts the conditioning of later blocks and inflates their denoising steps, so the saved compute reappears downstream. We present SAMR (Step-Aware Memory Reconstruction), a training-free method for frozen causal video DiTs that refreshes only part of the cache and reconstructs the rest without DiT forwards. Our key observation is that, once rotary position phases are removed, motion-aligned historical KV and the in-flight KV a token holds at its exit step are complementary estimates of its clean KV. SAMR debiases in-flight KV with offline-calibrated per-head affine maps in Pre-RoPE space, fuses the two estimates, and reserves true $t=0$ refreshes for tokens flagged by an attention-readout error proxy, all executed by tile-aligned, synchronization-free Triton kernels. On 48-second LongLive-1.3B videos, SAMR reduces DiT latency by 20.9% and principal FLOPs by 30.7% relative to dense KV updates, lowers downstream denoising steps, and improves final-quarter PSNR over token reuse by 1.61 dB (1.14 dB on held-out VidProM-16). The reconstruction also transfers to frozen Self-Forcing-DMD-1.3B: zero-shot, it reduces reuse-induced step inflation ($2.47 \to 2.30$ steps/token) and improves late PSNR by $+0.33$ dB, and a one-time training-free calibration recovers the diagnostic score that zero-shot transfer lowers ($89.62 \to 91.10$).

title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
authors: Dong Ji, Yunan Cui
abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_Φ$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $Δ_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

title: Infinite lower triangular matrices that are similar to their inverses but are not products of two involutions
authors: Pham The Nhan
abstract: Let $F$ be a field, and let $\GL_{\cf}(F)$ be the group of invertible column-finite matrices over $F$ indexed by $\bbN\times\bbN$. Denote by $\LT(F)$ (resp.\ $\UT(F)$) the subgroup consisting of lower (resp.\ upper) triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are equal to $1$. Every matrix in $\UT(F)$ is a product of two involutions. We show that, if $F$ has at least four elements, then $\LT(F)$ contains a matrix which is conjugate to its inverse by an invertible lower triangular matrix, but is not a product of two involutions in $\GL_{\cf}(F)$. The matrices can be chosen to be $4$-periodic. This gives a negative answer to a conjecture of de Seguins Pazzis.

title: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning enhanced Federated Learning for Predicting Remaining Useful Lifetime
authors: Rajarshi Chattopadhyay, Chen-Khong Tham
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is central to Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). The growth of industrial IoT has unlocked large multivariate sensor streams and enabled deep models - especially Transformers - for long-horizon sequence learning. However, transformers are parameter-heavy and data-hungry, while operational datasets are often siloed and privacy-sensitive. Federated Learning (FL) addresses this by training across clients without raw data sharing, but in practice many clients connect over lossy wireless links where UDP is preferred for low latency, making model exchange vulnerable to packet drops. We present a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that adapts FL to lossy channels by selecting per-client layer subsets to transmit and capping retransmissions. This framework is trained with QMIX value-function factorization for scalability. We instantiate the approach with a Graph Convolution Position-Aware Transformer (GCPATr) for RUL forecasting. On the CMAPSS dataset, our MARL-enhanced FL (RL-FL) consistently improves mean square error over standard FL, with the largest gains at high packet loss (e.g., up to 18% improvement on FD003 at 50% loss). These results show that MARL is an effective countermeasure to wireless degradation in FL-based RUL prediction.

title: Don't Miss the Forest for the Trees: Zero-Shot Skeleton Action Recognition with Hyperbolic Hierarchical Semantic Prototypes
authors: Zixiao Jin, Siyu Zhu, Feng Ding, Haisheng Fu, Xin Dong, Shankai Chen, Jie Liang
abstract: Zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition is evaluated almost exclusively on flat leaf labels, which leaves open whether a representation also grounds the broader concepts that contain an action in skeleton motion. We find that strong leaf alignment does not carry over to them: when ancestor concepts are scored directly under independent decoding, eight flat methods with 57.86-73.29% mean leaf Top-1 reach only 6.15-31.21% mean full-path accuracy across four NTU RGB+D splits. We propose the Hyperbolic Hierarchical Semantic Prototype ($H^2SP$) framework, which represents every node of an action taxonomy in the Lorentz model of hyperbolic space. First, instead of learning a free vector per node, $H^2SP$ synthesizes hierarchy-aware prototypes by recursive parent-child geodesic interpolation under a single tree-wide gate. Second, tangent-space semantic and distributional alignment on seen classes anchor the leaf prototypes in skeleton motion. Third, a soft entailment-cone regularizer encourages directional parent-child inclusion, propagating this motion grounding to ancestor concepts. We evaluate hierarchical concept prediction under independent and cascade decoding, and transfer to an alternative taxonomy without retraining. Across the four splits, $H^2SP$ attains the best mean independent and cascade full-path accuracy among the evaluated methods, at a comparable leaf Top-1 of 72.40%. Transferred to the alternative taxonomy, it outperforms both flat baselines and the same-tree Euclidean control across every split and decoding mode, indicating that its concept-level correspondence extends beyond the training taxonomy.

title: AgentDRC: Multi-Agent Algorithms for Spatially-Aware Automated DRC Correction
authors: Pengju Liu, Nuo Xu, Winso Chen, Peijun Li, Yang, Zhao, Yu Cao, Caiwen Ding
abstract: Design Rule Checking (DRC) error fixing remains a time-consuming bottleneck in physical design, often requiring manual intervention despite advanced EDA optimizations. Existing LLM-agent approaches fall short due to redundant contextual shapes, limited spatial reasoning over raw coordinates, and inefficient flat layout representations. We propose AgentDRC, which formulates iterative DRC correction as a multi-agent algorithm and introduces a spatial-aware verification and correction algorithm that reconstructs structured spatial relations among critical shapes and validates fixes through geometric and semantic constraint checking. The system coordinates four specialized agents to perceive multi-level, multi-modal geometric features, filter irrelevant shapes, and iteratively correct violations. Experiments show that AgentDRC achieves up to 30.4% pass@1 and 55.7% pass@5 on challenging violations, with 13.8% pass@5 improvement over the best baseline. We will open-source all code and benchmark tasks upon acceptance.

title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
authors: Zhifei Zhu, Hongtao Zhang, Yu Ren, Wei Zhou, Zeping Xie, Yi He
abstract: EEG analysis spans choosing alternatives, judging statements, and rating ordered attributes, requiring calibratable probabilities with explicit meaning. We present EEG-Jev, a unified single-pass decision model for EEG. Given an EEG window, a question and an answer specification, one forward pass returns a typed readout: CHOICE gives a candidate distribution, NOUL a proposition probability, and SCORE an ordered-level distribution and expectation. One checkpoint is trained jointly and evaluated once on held-out splits of 35 public sources. Core raw outputs reach 54.08% balanced accuracy on Stieger2021 motor imagery, 70.45% on Sleep-EDF-SC sleep staging, 72.11% per window at threshold 0.5 on CHB-MIT seizure detection with 0.825 AUROC, and 1.700 MAE on 0-10 ds005292 pain ratings. Prior correction and temperature scaling lower negative log-likelihood from 0.766 to 0.606 on Sleep-EDF-SC and 0.166 to 0.019 on CHB-MIT, while direct readout cuts batch-1 latency from 122.43 to 63.11 ms (1.94-fold) against a matched-backbone generative comparator. Interactive demonstration and aggregate results: https://neuroimglab.github.io/EEG-Jev/.

title: Upper and lower bounds for the critical point of the three-dimensional Ising model
authors: Zhongpu Qiu
abstract: We prove that the critical point $K_c$ of the nearest-neighbour Ising ferromagnet on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ satisfies $0.2164203058<K_c<0.2293910295$, equivalently $1.541630483<e^{2K_c}<1.582145851$, with both endpoints given by explicit rational numbers. To our knowledge these are the sharpest rigorous bounds available. They improve the classical bounds of Fisher (1967) and of Fröhlich, Simon and Spencer (1976), narrowing the rigorously known interval by a factor of about 3.5, and the interval contains the numerical estimate of the critical point. For the lower bound we refine Fisher's self-avoiding-walk argument. A shortest path in the high-temperature expansion forbids all bonds spanned by its vertices, and the resulting gain is estimated through local correlation integrals and summed over paths by a finite-memory transfer bound. As a by-product, the connective constant of $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is shown to be at most $4.73195$. For the upper bound we prove an infrared bound whose coefficient involves the nearest-neighbour correlation. We keep the zero Fourier mode as an unknown and force it to be positive by exact local relations for the spins on a small shell. The finite inequalities entering the proof are verified in exact rational arithmetic, and the passage to the thermodynamic limit is proved analytically.

title: A dedicated survey of fast-rotating near-Earth asteroids with the Two-meter Twin Telescope. II. Tumblers
authors: M. R. Alarcon, D. J. Scheeres, J. Licandro, C. J. Benson, M. Serra-Ricart
abstract: Fast rotation dominates the metre- to decametre-size near-Earth asteroid (NEA) population, but the incidence of non-principal-axis (NPA) rotation, or tumbling, in this regime is essentially unconstrained. We establish how common NPA rotation is among small, fast-rotating NEAs, how its prevalence varies with size, and what it implies for the internal structure and recent dynamical history of these bodies. We analysed the homogeneous high-cadence sample obtained with the Two-meter Twin Telescope at Teide Observatory and presented in the first paper of this series. Light curves showing coherent residual structure under a single-frequency Fourier model were refitted with a bivariate Fourier series in two independent frequencies, and dynamical modes were assigned from the normalised harmonic amplitude spectrum. We confirm 32 NPA rotators, 14 with both periods reliably resolved, with periods spanning 0.48-46.4 min and estimated diameters of 7-140 m. The most extreme object with both periods resolved, 2025 FB8 (shortest period $P_1 = 71$ s, estimated diameter $D \simeq 7$ m), is the fastest and smallest such tumbler characterised to date. Eight objects satisfy our harmonic quality criteria, and all eight are consistent with long-axis mode rotation. The tumbler fraction among fast rotators is 16.0 %, rising from 13.8 % at absolute magnitude $H < 26$ to 22.5 % at $H \geq 26$. Twenty-three of the 32 lie above the spin limit of a cohesionless rubble pile; none exceeds the lunar-regolith limit. Tumbling is common among small fast rotators, with no evidence that it becomes rarer towards the smallest sizes. Fast tumblers require modest cohesion but no monolithic interior, occupying the same structural domain as their principal-axis counterparts.

title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
authors: Sajjad Pakdamansavoji
abstract: Robots must often keep working after the world changes, as when a block moves or the camera shifts while the robot still acts on what it saw before. Recent work showed that one change during a task lowers success for every policy tested, but did not separate the effect of its timing from the cost of the changed world, or measure what it costs afterwards. We introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases on CALVIN's five-instruction chains, each with one change to the objects, the camera, the robot, or the instruction. Each case compares three runs that are identical until the affected instruction begins: one without the change, one with it in place from that moment, and one in which it arrives while the robot is moving. The second run against the first gives the cost of the changed world, and the third against the second the effect of meeting it mid-motion. On 1,526 held-out cases per policy, with hypotheses fixed in advance, each of ten released policies loses 4.4 to 9.9 percentage points on the affected instruction over the eight core changes. Whether timing matters depends on the change: one that alters what the robot sees costs 5.4 points less mid-motion than from the start, whereas a change to the scene itself or to the robot shows no detectable effect. Rewinding the robot to the start of the instruction removes the benefit for every policy; the stricter test we fixed in advance, that the rewound run then matches the second run, passes for three. The cost also outlasts the affected instruction: the change stays in place, and a policy that still completes that instruction is 5.0 to 16.8 points less likely to complete the next one.

title: Sharp Poincaré-Wirtinger Inequalities on Finite Graphs
authors: Chenghao Xiang, Fayou Zhao
abstract: Let $G_n=(V_{G_n},E_{G_n})$ be the finite connected graph with $n\geq3$ vertices. We study the sharp constant $C_{G_n,p}$ such that the Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality \[ \Vert f-m_f\Vert_p\leq C_{G_n,p} {\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}(f) \] holds for every $f$ on $V$, where ${\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}$ stands for the $p$-variation on $G_n$ and $m_f$ stands for the arithmetic mean of $f$. For complete graphs, the optimal constant is known for $p\in[1,3+δ_n^1)\cup(3+δ_n^2,+\infty)$, with $δ_n^1=\frac{1}{2n^2\ln n}+O(1/n^3)$ and $δ_n^2=\frac{2}{n}+O(1/n^2)$. In this paper, we firstly extend the admissible range to all $p\in(0,\infty)$. Secondly, we obtain the sharp constant $C_{S_n,p}$ for the star graph $S_n$ in the range $p\in(0,+\infty)$ and give estimates for the sharp constant $C_{P_n,p}$ on path graphs when $p\in(0,+\infty)$. Thirdly, we characterize the extremizers on complete graphs and star graphs, and establish the existence of monotone extremizers on path graphs for $p\in(0,+\infty)$. For path graphs, we obtain explicit sharp constants for $p\in(0,1]\cup\{2\}$, and interpolation upper bounds for $p\in(1,+\infty)$. We also prove that for any finite connected graph $G_n$, the best constant at $p=+\infty$ is exactly its remoteness. Moreover, for general finite connected graphs $G_n$ and $p\in(0,+\infty)$, we establish optimal bounds for $C_{G_n,p}$; the complete graph uniquely attains the lower bound for all $p>0$; the path graph attains the upper bound for $p>1$, but for $0<p\leq1$ there exist nonpath graphs that attain the same supremum. Finally, we show that our approach yields sharper upper bounds than the path-based estimates obtained via the Cheeger constant.

title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
authors: Avi Aggarwal, Yiran Hu
abstract: SWE-bench-style benchmarks, such as SWE-bench Verified (Verified) and SWE-bench Pro (Pro), evaluate coding agents with tests taken from the change that originally fixed each issue. However, these tests can enforce details the task never states, causing correct alternative fixes to fail. Such overspecified tests have so far been found mainly through expensive expert review. To address this, we define the Spec-Test Coverage Gap (STCG), a 1-4 scale measuring overspecification, and score it with two LLM judges, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, which are given the specification and the test patch. A task is flagged as overspecified when both judges score it 3 or higher. Our study has three parts. First, we validate the judges on 206 tasks that earlier human audits and agent results label as overspecified or fine. Second, we apply STCG to all 500 Verified and 731 public Pro tasks and compare the flags with the results of the top 30 Verified submissions. Third, we verify the flags by asking Claude Opus 5.5 to loosen the overspecified requirements of flagged tasks, and regrade 2,186 failed patches from those submissions. Our main findings are: (1) Overspecified tests are detectable: on the validation tasks, the judges correctly flag 89% of the tasks that human audits identify as overspecified and wrongly flag only 4% of the tasks known to be fine. (2) Overspecified tests are common: applied to whole benchmarks, the judges flag 23% of Verified and 35% of Pro tasks. (3) Flagged tasks are much harder for agents: the top 30 Verified submissions resolve only 31% of the flagged tasks on average, against 88% of the other tasks. (4) Overspecified tests change the leaderboard: relaxing the tests lets 61% of the 2,186 failed patches on flagged tasks pass. Counting these patches as resolved would add 33 to 60 tasks to each top-30 submission, raising resolve rates by up to 12 percentage points.

title: Phase-Resolved X-ray Polarimetry of LMC X-1: Enhanced Polarization at Inferior Conjunction
authors: Yu-Shan Ling, Fei Xie, Alessandro Di Marco, Fabio La Monaca
abstract: We present a phase-resolved X-ray polarimetric analysis of the extragalactic black hole X-ray binary LMC X-1, a classical high/soft state source with a well-characterized accretion disk and an ionization cone/inferred jet. Previous X-ray polarimetry gave only orbit-averaged upper limits on the polarization fraction, leaving any orbital-phase dependence unexplored. We aim to probe how this polarization depends on orbital phase and to identify the origin of the polarized emission. We analyzed simultaneous IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR observations taken in October 2022. We measured the polarization degree and angle in different energy bands as a function of orbital phase, performed spectro-polarimetric modeling to identify the emitting components, and modeled the phase modulation of the Stokes parameters with a cosine function. The polarization depends on orbital phase: during inferior conjunction (phase from -0.1 to 0.1), the polarization degree is (4.2+/-1.1)% in 2-3 keV and (3.4+/-0.8)% in 2-8 keV, with polarization angles of (46+/-8) and (50+/-7) degrees. Outside this phase it stays below the 99% minimum detectable polarization. The measured angle agrees with the ionization cone/jet direction (~45 degrees), and spectro-polarimetric modeling favors a soft-band origin for the polarization. The Stokes Q/I and U/I modulation is well described by a cosine at the orbital period and favors two spatially separated polarized components over a single one varying in amplitude. We also tested whether differential Faraday rotation of the disk light in an ordered magnetic field can reproduce the modulation and used it to place upper limits on the magnetic field. These results show that soft-band polarization of LMC X-1 appears only near inferior conjunction at a position angle aligned with the disk normal, and highlight the importance of orbital-phase sampling in polarimetric studies.

title: Interface and film engineering for improved spin-charge interconversion in sputtered GeTe nanodevices
authors: S. Teresi, T. Frottier, M. Culot, W. Savero-Torres, P. Sgarro, M. Wissmann, A. Kandazoglou, F. Osana, J. Lagrave, D. Térébénec, J. Paterson, A. Oysel Mestre, O. J. Mouawad, E. Chevilley, N. Bernier, P. Noé, M. Bibes, F. Hippert, J. -P. Attané, L. Vila, M. Cosset-Chéneau
abstract: Spin-logic devices promise non-volatile logic-in-memory computing with ultra-low power consumption, offering a route to circumvent the von Neumann bottleneck. Magnetoelectric and ferroelectric spin-orbit (MESO/FESO) devices, however, require spin-charge interconversion materials that combine a large output signal with properties that survive nanoscale integration. Tellurides are particularly fragile in this respect, as processing readily introduces defects that degrade their spin-charge interconversion properties. Here we demonstrate room-temperature spin-charge interconversion in patterned FESO nanoscale devices based on sputtered GeTe, with feature sizes down to 100 nm. By introducing a Ti interfacial layer between the CoFe electrode and GeTe, and by using GeTe films of improved crystalline quality, we increase the interconversion output signal from 3 mΩ to 24 mΩ, exceeding values reported for platinum at comparable device size. These results establish large-scale-deposited GeTe as a viable material platform for spin-logic devices and identify interface quality and film crystallinity as key levers for optimizing their performance.

title: Beyond the Benchmark: Localizing Released Autonomous Driving Models to Real Vehicles
authors: Morui Zhu, Deyuan Qu, Qi Chen, Qing Yang
abstract: Released autonomous-driving models achieve strong benchmark performance, yet deploying them on a new real vehicle remains challenging. We study this deployment gap and find that released models can remain coupled to assumptions from their source sensing, data, and execution processes even after conventional adaptation. We introduce Released-to-Real (R2R), a deployment-localization methodology that identifies such source-system coupling and corrects only the affected components while preserving the released model. For data and behavior adaptation, we find that the mismatch between trajectory-level optimization and receding-horizon execution enters through the ego state rather than the observation, and introduce Human-Anchored Reinforcement Learning (HA-RL), which corrects it on recorded target driving without the costly rollouts of generative closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL). For physical sensor adaptation, R2R localizes and corrects source-dependent spatial and temporal representations with frozen perception weights, requiring neither target annotations nor retraining. HA-RL improves the closed-loop success rate of a released diffusion-based planner from 82.2% to 95.2%, while sensor adaptation across multiple released detectors and three real sensor rigs improves the vehicle mean average precision (mAP) of a released multi-camera detector from 0.041 to 0.420 on a five-camera target rig. These results provide a practical path for preparing released models before deployment on new real vehicles. Our project page is publicly available at https://released-to-real.github.io.

title: Gradient-free MCMC exploiting low-dimensional Gaussian and nonGaussian posterior structure
authors: Hongqiao Wang, Jiahua Jiang, Jing Liu, Jinglai Li
abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for Bayesian inverse problems is expensive: the unknown is high-dimensional, every likelihood evaluation requires a forward solve, and gradients are often unavailable. The posterior typically differs from the prior in a few directions and is often approximately Gaussian in most of them but strongly non-Gaussian in a few. We propose the NQU sampler, a gradient-free MCMC method that splits the parameter space into non-Gaussian (N), approximately quadratic (Q) and uninformative (U) directions. The split is learned once, before sampling, from likelihood values, and each block is updated by a kernel suited to it; a collapsed update handles a global prior scale. Because the learned structure only shapes the proposals, every update leaves the exact posterior invariant, at the cost of one likelihood evaluation. We give a condition under which the blocks can be learned and show that, for likelihoods with exactly the learned structure, the spectral gap of the sampler does not depend on the dimension, whereas updating the scale given all coordinates can have a gap of order $1/d$. On the posterior axes, the NQU sampler, learning included, needed the fewest evaluations in four of five synthetic examples with $d=200$, among nine baselines including gradient-based ones; in those with non-Gaussian directions, gradient-free baselines needed at least ten times as many. On a methane ignition problem with 219 uncertain rate constants, it gave consistent estimates, whereas full-space robust adaptive Metropolis needed about 300 times as many evaluations and an ensemble sampler degenerated.

title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Selector for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
authors: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Junhyeok Kang, Jaehoon Lee, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn
abstract: Recent time-series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast a distribution over futures, and multimodal time-series (TS) forecasting further exploits other modalities to improve forecasting accuracy. However, existing works have two limitations: 1) TSFMs reduce the predictive distribution to its median or mean, flattening diverse futures into a calm line, and 2) multimodal TS forecasting models incorporate text into the forecaster through TS-language alignment, which is substantially weaker than vision-language alignment. To address these limitations, we propose the VIsion-language SelectOR (VISOR), a multimodal TS forecasting framework that selects one plausible future instead of averaging across candidates, leveraging the alignment capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to select the most suitable candidate based on textual information. VISOR consists of two components: 1) a text-free stochastic predictor that samples diverse candidate futures, and 2) a VLM selector that reads the candidates as a single chart image and selects one based on the text. To avoid overly calm forecasting paths, we train the selector with a shape-aware target that evaluates each candidate based on both point-wise error and path shape. Across three benchmarks covering ten datasets, VISOR achieves the best average ranking in both point and volatility errors compared with TSFMs and multimodal TS forecasting models. Code: https://github.com/seunghan96/VISOR.

title: ReCAP: Sequential Concept Acquisition with Guarantees under Imperfect Concept Predictors
authors: Md Nahiduzzaman, Steven Korevaar, Alireza Bab-Hadiashar, Ruwan Tennakoon
abstract: Sequential concept acquisition enables interpretable diagnosis from a compact set of human-understandable findings. Such explanations are useful only if clinicians can trust them, yet most existing methods treat predicted concepts as correct, so a correct diagnosis can rest on incorrectly predicted evidence. We propose Reliable Concept Acquisition with Pruning (ReCAP), which reasons over what the concept predictor reports, including errors and abstentions, and replaces conditional information gain with a label-discriminating objective that separates cases requiring different diagnoses. We prove this objective adaptively monotone and adaptively submodular, yielding a (1-1/e) guarantee for greedy fixed-budget acquisition that degrades boundedly under learned estimates, and combine it with abstention-aware acquisition and diagnosis-preserving pruning to keep explanations short and reliable. Across five medical imaging datasets, ReCAP reduces the share of correct diagnoses supported by at least one incorrectly predicted concept from 27.1% to 9.6% relative to the strongest baseline, while using fewer than half as many concepts and achieving higher diagnostic accuracy.

title: Bounds on the Distance of Subgradient Trajectories to the Optimal Set
authors: Nicholas Dwork, Charles Tsao, Jorge Balbas, Cody Coleman, John M. Pauly
abstract: A subgradient method with a constant step size may reach a minimizer and subsequently move away from it. Thus, a bound on the best objective value does not characterize the remainder of the trajectory. In this manuscript, we first establish that the trajectory enters a near-optimal sublevel set in finitely many iterations. We then use the Hausdorff distance between this sublevel set and the optimal set to bound the distance of every subsequent iterate from the optimal set. For objectives with weak sharp minima, we derive a tighter bound and construct examples demonstrating that the bound is tight. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results and illustrate when the bounds are conservative.

title: Dreamcatcher: Remembering What Surprises a World Model in Video Streams
authors: Jinxi He, Ce Zhang, Wenhe Liu, Jianshu Zhang, Katia P. Sycara, Yaqi Xie
abstract: As live video streams grow longer, repeatedly encoding and processing their full histories becomes increasingly costly. Answering questions as they arrive therefore calls for visual memory built in one pass before future questions are known. Existing methods mainly keep tokens that differ from earlier ones or match surrogate queries fixed in advance. Without modeling world dynamics, these criteria struggle to tell subtle surprising details from expected change. We introduce Dreamcatcher, a training-free framework and, to our knowledge, the first to use predictive signals from an independently pretrained, frozen video world model for online memory formation in streaming video question answering. Conditioned on recent history, the world model predicts incoming features using learned world priors. Its normalized prediction errors yield temporal and spatial surprisal signals that guide online segmentation and the retention of a frozen Video-LLM's native visual tokens, balancing surprising details with broad visual coverage under budgets that decay with segment age. At query time, an evidence gate admits a segment from a similarity-based shortlist only when the Video-LLM judges that it adds evidence for the question beyond the current view. We evaluate Dreamcatcher on three streaming and three offline long-video benchmarks. On OVO-Bench, Dreamcatcher achieves the highest overall accuracy among the compared training-free methods for each of four frozen Video-LLMs, reaching 78.9% with Qwen3.8-27B. With the three Qwen Video-LLMs, it also reduces average input tokens for answer generation by more than 80% relative to their base models at 1 fps.

title: Gaussian Process Data-Driven Hamiltonian for Probabilistic Safe Set Construction
authors: Seungseok Oh, Junho Kim, Jason J. Choi, Namhoon Cho
abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability is a general framework for verifying the safety of nonlinear systems, but it relies on an accurate dynamics model. The data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH) framework avoids system identification by lower-bounding the Hamiltonian directly from state-control-velocity data. However, it requires a Lipschitz bound on the unknown dynamics which is hard to certify from finite data, and as a single global constant this bound makes the computed safe sets conservative. We propose the Gaussian process data-driven Hamiltonian (GP-DDH), a fully data-driven framework that constructs safe sets with probabilistic guarantees under a GP prior on the dynamics. Furthermore, we suggest two methods to choose the confidence parameter $β$, both mathematically guaranteed to underbound the Hamiltonian. The computed safe set lies inside the true one with posterior probability at least $1-Δ$ for any $Δ\in(0,1)$. Numerical experiments show that GP-DDH recovers a bigger volume of the true safe set than DDH while still correctly providing a conservative approximation, even when DDH is given a Lipschitz constant computed from the true dynamics.

title: The VC-Dimension of Visibility in Simple Polygons Is Six
authors: Dror Aiger, Sariel Har-Peled
abstract: Six targets in a simple polygon can be placed so that, for every subset of the targets, some point in the polygon sees precisely that subset---that is, the polygon shatters the six targets. We prove that no simple polygon shatters seven targets. Together with Valtr's six-target construction, this determines the maximum visibility VC-dimension of a simple polygon to be six (even when the targets must lie in strictly convex position) and improves the previous upper bound of $14$ due to Gilbers and Klein. To rule out a shattered set of seven targets, we classify its convex-hull structure into $74$ cases. In each case, the absence of holes in the polygon forces visibility relations that we encode as Boolean constraints on links and triple orientations. Independently checkable SAT refutations exclude all $74$ cases. The upper-bound proof was derived using AI. A separate Lean 4 formalization independently verifies the upper bound against an axiomatic interface for simple polygons.

title: Normal edge-transitive bi-Cayley graphs of prime valency over nonabelian simple groups
authors: Zai Ping Lu, Hai Ze Wang
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a connected graph of prime valency admitting a nonabelian simple group $R$ that acts semiregularly on the vertices with exactly two orbits. We prove that if the normalizer of $R$ in $Aut(Γ)$ is edge-transitive, then $Γ$ is bipartite and $R$ is characteristic in $Aut(Γ)$. We derive consequences for Cayley graphs and a criterion for semisymmetry. As an application, we construct bi-Cayley graphs over $A_p$ from the conjugates of a $3$-cycle under a cyclic group of order $p$, where $p>5$ is prime. These graphs are semisymmetric precisely when the support of the $3$-cycle is not a three-term arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{F}_p$.

title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents
authors: Ilia Hashemi Rad, Feijie Wu, Haoyu Wang, Jing Gao
abstract: The growing autonomy of AI agents in using external tools and making decisions has created an urgent need for comprehensive safety benchmarks. Existing benchmarks test compromised tool channels or adaptive multi-turn attacks, though they may not capture the unique capabilities of policy-governed tool-use agents, which must resist unauthorized requests without abandoning the legitimate work embedded in the same interaction. To fill this gap, we introduce TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark built around scenario-specific stories, personas, manipulation tactics, and response-adaptive escalation. Each adversarial task targets an action explicitly prohibited by the policy provided to the assistant, while the policy remains hidden from the attacking user. TACT pairs each adversarial task with at least one benign counterpart, and its adversarial tasks retain authorized ground-truth actions when a compliant resolution remains available. We define these base tasks as TACT-Base. We additionally introduce TACT-TrustPrime, which places an independent benign task before an unrelated attack in the same conversation. We also propose Paired Selective Trustworthiness (PST), which combines explicit safe refusal with demonstrated capability on matched benign tasks, to analyze an agent's overcautiousness and practicality. Averaged across 6 different models as assistants, TACT-Base raises Attack-Induced Failure Rate (AFR) by 17.53% over four compatible attack baselines, and TACT-TrustPrime raises it by a further 17.01%. The two evaluated defense methods reduce AFR by only 8.35%--9.41% on average and do not consistently improve PST, underscoring the need for stronger policy-enforcement methods.

title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
authors: Mari Carmen Bañuls, Krzysztof Cichy, C. -J. David Lin, Manuel Schneider
abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.

title: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations
authors: Zeyan Li, Jianfeng Xu
abstract: Expert pruning reduces the memory footprint of mixture-of-experts language models, but retaining model quality depends on which experts are removed. Frequency- and magnitude-based scores measure the expert in isolation and overlook how normalization consumes its contribution: subtracting one expert changes both the direction of the residual stream and the scale applied to what remains. We propose FN-Prune, a training-free criterion that compares the next RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, holding original routes and weights fixed. Squared differences are averaged over all calibration tokens in one pass; low-scoring experts are physically deleted at uniform per-layer ratios, and inference reroutes among survivors. At 50% expert removal, FN-Prune achieves lower WikiText-2 perplexity than the best published methods on Qwen3, ERNIE, and OLMoE, including a 32% reduction on OLMoE. At the same budget, GSM8K accuracy improves over the best published methods by 7.5 and 7.0 percentage points on Qwen3 and ERNIE, respectively, while multiple-choice gains remain task-dependent.

title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
authors: Juan Hormaza, Wenyang Qian
abstract: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.

title: Asymptotic Normality of the Pearson Correlation between Two Weakly Dependent Random Fields
authors: Jiyue Qin, Armin Schwartzman, Samuel Davenport
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the sample Pearson correlation coefficient between two weakly dependent random fields on a lattice of any fixed dimension. Under strict stationarity, $(BL,θ)$-weak dependence and mild moment conditions, we establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimator on regularly growing domains, which need not be rectangular, with an asymptotic variance expressed through joint fourth-order moments. When the correlation is zero, asymptotic normality holds under weaker conditions. When the fields are independent, the asymptotic variance simplifies to a sum over spatial lags of products of their autocorrelations. The variance approximations behind the classic modified $t$-test, although derived for independent Gaussian fields, target the right variance even without Gaussianity. We also give sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality that are easy to check and cover bounded, Gaussian, $m$-dependent and independent fields. For Gaussian fields, summable auto- and cross-covariances suffice. These conditions rely on new closure results. Squares and products, although not Lipschitz, preserve $(BL,θ)$-dependence for Gaussian fields, and products of independent fields do so when one is positively or negatively associated. Finally, we propose kernel-based estimators of the asymptotic variance, enabling inference without Gaussianity or parametric spatial models. Simulation studies illustrate their finite-sample performance.

title: DAA for an Autonomous Delivery Drone: Maneuver Selection Policies for Near-Collision Risk Avoidance
authors: Franco Callari, Ishay Kamon, Anthony Narkawitz, Pradeep Yarlagadda, Amir Navot
abstract: Detect-and-avoid (DAA) systems for autonomous drones operating in shared airspace must select avoidance maneuvers under conditions that differ markedly from those assumed by conventional DAA architectures designed for crewed aircraft. Limited on-board sensing capabilities restrict detection of collision risk to near distances (sub-km), the time available for decision-making is severely limited, uncertainty in the predicted closest point of approach (CPA) and the time to reach it is substantial, and the maneuver envelope of a small uncrewed aircraft at low altitude is tightly constrained. This paper presents and compares two maneuver-selection strategies that address these challenges: (1) a purely geometric approach, steering in the direction away from the intruder at CPA, and (2) a method that also takes into account the known sources of uncertainty in the intruder's location, and steers away from a plane expected to contain the intruder's location distribution at CPA. Performance is evaluated using the risk ratio metric on a large dataset of simulated near-collision encounters with crewed intruders. Results indicate that both strategies are feasible (i.e., computable in closed form from an onboard track estimate), and that the second strategy substantially outperforms the first.

title: fork() for Agents: Agent Kernel for Non-blocking LLM Orchestration
authors: Ankit Chadha, Pratyay Banerjee
abstract: LLM-based agents typically execute tool calls synchronously and discard completed work upon failure. Subgraph-selective recovery, re-executing only a failed node's transitive descendants, is a well-established pattern in distributed systems (Spark, Erlang/OTP, Dryad), and recent agent runtimes (Sherlock, AgentGit, Atomix) preserve completed work through verifiers, version control, or transactional tool boundaries. We present \textbf{Agent-Kernel}, a non-blocking runtime that ports this pattern to the LLM \emph{content plane}: its primitive, \textbf{Sub-Graph Recovery (SGR)}, fires on a raw exception with no trained verifier or planner, resets a failed node's descendants while preserving completed siblings, and composes each parent's text into its children's prompts (context inheritance), all on a durable substrate with a formal state-preservation guarantee. Across 14{,}434 runs on synthetic and standard benchmarks (tau-bench, Gaia2, AutomationBench, InterruptBench), SGR reaches full recovery within budget=3 where whole-trajectory replay exhausts (100\% vs.\ 55\%), and is roughly 10$\times$ faster than an adapted Sherlock rollback that also recovers. It matches ReAct-serial accuracy within noise on linear workloads while adding recovery and parallelism (up to 12.7$\times$ speedup) where structure permits. Ablation isolates SGR: removing it collapses success to 39.4\%.

title: Concentration of the half-space Airy line ensembles
authors: Jiaoyang Huang, Zongrui Yang
abstract: The half-space Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{hs};\varpi}$ ($\varpi\in\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$), introduced in arXiv:2505.01798, arXiv:2601.04546, are natural analogues of the Airy line ensemble and are expected to arise as universal scaling limits of models in the half-space Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) class. We prove that, at each fixed time $t\geq 0$, the height of the $k$th curve concentrates about $-(3πk/2)^{2/3}$ on the scale $k^{-1/3}\sqrt{\log(2+k)}$, with exponential tails.

title: Electron versus positron impact ionization of inner shells of heavy atoms: distortion, exchange and relativistic effects
authors: Colm T. Whelan
abstract: Triple differential cross sections are presented for electron and positron impact ionization of the K shells of Cu, Ag, Au and U and the L shells of Ag. Relativistic effects are important throughout. For positrons the recoil maximum is suppressed and the recoil-region spin asymmetry changes sign; for the $2s$ shell the binary peak changes. In symmetric geometry, where theory reproduces the measured absolute electron cross section, the positron peak lies on the other side of zero recoil. Measurements would test relativistic ionization theory in a regime that electron experiments cannot reach.

title: NOBODY Was There: Bridging the Human-VLM Gap in Unwarranted Person Attribution Bias
authors: Parsa Madinei, Ziqi Wen, Miguel Eckstein
abstract: Describing an image requires not only recognizing what is visible but deciding what should be inferred. We investigate a systematic gap between humans and VLMs in their tendency to attribute visible actions or events to people who are not present in an image. We term this behavior unwarranted person attribution bias and find that, across 25 SOTA VLMs, captions of person-absent scenes mention a person four times as often as human-written captions of the same images. Through a preference study, we further show that both humans and VLMs prefer captions that avoid such attributions. Motivated by this, we introduce NOBODY, a preference dataset designed to bridge the gap between humans and VLMs in unwarranted person attribution. Through direct preference optimization (DPO), we align open VLMs on NOBODY and show that their agreement with human captions on person attribution reaches or exceeds inter-human agreement, whereas nine existing public preference datasets leave this behavior largely unchanged. Furthermore, we show that human judges preferred the aligned VLM captions significantly more than those of the baseline model. Alongside NOBODY, we release NOBODY-Bench, which evaluates VLMs for unwarranted person attribution bias and their alignment against human captions and preference. Project page: https://pmadinei.github.io/NOBODY/

title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
authors: Phanuel Mariano, Jing Wang
abstract: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math.
