QBS organizes native-block format processing, block traversal, integer computation, and ordered FP32 accumulation into a unified execution process, whereas AKV maintains local K/V residency and supplies operand views aligned with the computation direction while leaving Attention arithmetic on RVV. Cycle-accurate RTL evaluation shows that QBS achieves geometric-mean speedups of 35.68x and 51.34x for projection Compute and Matmul, respectively, while AKV achieves a 1.45x geometric-mean speedup over Tiled RVV for Decode Attention. Compared with the baseline, the complete design increases total area by 12.65%; on the evaluated projection workloads, throughput per area and energy efficiency improve by 46.63x and 19.78x, respectively. Further evaluation demonstrates applicability across multiple block-quantization formats and across models with different Attention organizations.

title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
authors: Rezwana Razzaque Angana, Brendan Harding, Dimitrios Mitsotakis
abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior. In particular, to describe the properties of these traveling waves, we analyze heteroclinic orbits that connect two distinct equilibria, one of which undergoes a transition in the four-dimensional phase space from a saddle-focus to a saddle point as the dissipation parameter increases. This transition governs the nature of the wave profile, which evolves smoothly from an oscillatory shock wave to a regularized (non-oscillatory) shock wave. To compute such solutions, we introduce a finite-difference-based numerical method tailored for this class of problems.

title: Shuttle: Dependency-Attributed Workflow Evolution for Smart Contract Auditing
authors: Yue Xue, Yi Rong, Ziqiao Kong, Ronghui Gu, Dan She, Yuannan Yang, Zhiju Yang, Yuqiang Sun
abstract: In LLM-based smart contract auditing, detection quality depends on both model capability and workflow design. While coding agents can revise workflows from execution feedback, unconstrained rewrites rarely yield stable gains. Cross-function vulnerabilities require multi-step state tracking and boundary reasoning that coarse pipelines miss. End-to-end outcomes hide which step lost a clue, so direct rewrites regress existing hits or discard valid edits under coarse aggregate scoring. Repeatedly iterating on a small project set also adds case-specific heuristics that bloat prompts and hurt generalization. We present Shuttle, a constrained workflow-evolution system, and LucidScan, the auditing framework it evolves. Shuttle centers on provenance-graph attribution: it expands each run into an instance-level dependency graph, locates the node where a clue was lost via forward search, and traces existing hits backward into a protected set. After evaluating a merged batch, Shuttle drops dragging edits via a node-level provenance ledger, falling back to cache-reusing local re-runs only when early-round edits overlap on the same node. For localized bottlenecks, Shuttle generates edits under task decomposition, progressive refinement, and generality blind review. On 10 training projects, Shuttle evolves LucidScan from $G_0$ (28.7% per-project average C/H/M recall) to $G_8$ (82.1%). On 13 held-out validation projects under the same model, average recall rises from 28.6% ($G_0$) to 70.3% ($G_8$), above Pashov and Codex Security. In an anonymized live public audit contest with 896 researchers (Nov. 2026), the evolved scanner tied for #1 in High-severity recall (6/8, 75.0%), ranked #2 in scored H/M clusters (34/72, 47.2%) with 92.9% validity (78/84), and finished #3 overall.

title: (No) Separation of Concerns: Philosophical Concerns about Agent Ethics and Implications for SE Practitioners
authors: Marc Cheong, Sebastian Baltes, Joanne Byrne, Haoyu Gao, Raula Gaikovina Kula, Sarita Rosenstock, Christoph Treude, Mansooreh Zahedi
abstract: The use of AI agents in software engineering (SE) are commonplace, with differing levels of autonomy, a myriad of capabilities, and ability to perform a variety of tasks. Philosophers have begun to examine the ethics of such agents, and SE researchers or practitioners could benefit from them; on the other hand, SE practitioners currently explore most of these concerns through the lens of principlism. We bridge this gap by reviewing the philosophical literature on AI agents indexed in PhilPapers, and translating its ethical concerns into a research agenda for SE researchers and into implications for teams that use coding agents. A systematic mapping study of PhilPapers -- a major philosophy index and open access archive -- yielded 33 peer-reviewed papers by professional philosophers published since 2023. We coded these papers thematically, with cross-disciplinary review of the emerging themes, resulting in eight themes and 85 codes. From these, we derive seven research questions for SE, covering developers' reliance on agents, responsibility for agent-written code, ethical constraints in agent configurations, and benchmark design. For practitioners, we derive five implications: decide which choices an agent must refer to a human, keep agent-written pull requests small enough to review, pair configuration-file instructions with checks, watch for changes to tests, and record who approved what. We argue that ethical concerns cannot be separated from SE concerns into a module of their own: they arise inside code review, configuration, evaluation, and requirements work, and addressing them requires cross-disciplinary work.

title: Decompose, Verify, Evolve: Physically Grounded Shape Decomposition
authors: Wenchao Ma, Rui Yu, Fan Zhu, Jiachen Liu, Sharon X. Huang
abstract: Shape decomposition represents 3D objects as a compact set of geometric primitives for interpretable modeling and simulation. However, existing decomposition methods are trained primarily for geometric fidelity, without explicit constraints on physical plausibility, and can therefore produce disconnected parts or physically unstable reconstructions. We present PhysDec, an agentic framework that draws on a pretrained vision-language model's semantic understanding and commonsense reasoning to predict material-aware primitive decompositions from a few images. Within this framework, PhysDec-Loop is an agentic pipeline that reasons about part structure and materials, using a reference 3D point cloud for geometric feedback and physical verifiers to guide iterative refinement. Through self-evolution, we further develop another agentic pipeline, PhysDec-Evolved, which learns from prior corrections to predict primitive decompositions from images without point-cloud feedback or a correction loop at inference. Experiments show that PhysDec-Loop improves geometric fidelity, physical plausibility and visual quality over geometry-focused baselines, while PhysDec-Evolved approaches its performance at substantially lower inference cost.

title: Detecting Topological Phases Through Dynamics of Chiral Density in Momentum-space Lattices
authors: Rui Tian, Xiayao He, Tianhao Wu, Dongdong Pu, Shuai Li, Bo Liu
abstract: Momentum-space lattices offer a versatile platform for quantum simulation in particular emulating topological states of matter.In this work, we propose a spectroscopic protocol via utilizing the dynamics of the chiral operator to detect the topological properties of a momentum-space Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain. We show that the time evolution of the chiral density is directly linked to the local density of state (LDOS). By performing a Fourier transformation of that, we reconstruct both the LDOS and density of states of the system, enabling the unambiguous signature of zero-energy edge modes and the bulk-boundary correspondence. This dynamical approach provides a diagnostic tool for exploring topological phases in synthetic quantum matter.

title: Superconductivity with valley-imbalanced Fermi surfaces in thick rhombohedral graphene
authors: Le Liu, Jian Zhao, Cheng Xu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yang Zhang, Weibo Gao
abstract: Superconductivity in spin-polarized metals challenges conventional opposite-spin pairing, particularly when a magnetic field strengthens rather than suppresses it. In graphene, the additional valley degree of freedom broadens the possible pairing channels, making the valley occupation of the parent metal central to understanding such superconductivity. Here we report in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity in hBN-aligned 17-layer rhombohedral graphene. Normal-state quantum oscillations reveal unequal Fermi pockets consistent with a valley-imbalanced, spin-polarized parent metal. Calculations show that the parent electron pocket is predominantly localized on the bottom surface and largely preserved by electrostatic screening as additional Fermi pockets emerge. Superconductivity persists in this regime but is suppressed when carriers are polarized toward the hBN-aligned surface, where the parent bands undergo strong moire reconstruction. An adjacent nonlinear metallic response evolves continuously into superconducting critical-current features and persists above the superconducting transition temperature. The combination of valley imbalance and in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity motivates a phenomenological magnon-assisted equal-spin intervalley pairing scenario. These findings provide experimental constraints on pairing in valley-imbalanced metals and open a route to testing magnetic pairing mechanisms through layer-selective control of the parent electronic states.

title: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
authors: Jiaming Zhang, Yao Lyu, Haoning Wang, Yongjun Chen, Liping Zhang, Shengbo Eben Li
abstract: Large-scale pretraining provides embodied models with general capabilities, but reliable task execution still requires post training. In multitask settings, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) faces distribution mismatch between training and deployment, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) is limited by sparse rewards and uneven learning progress across tasks. Multi-teacher on policy distillation (MOPD) consolidates expert capabilities through dense supervision on the model's own trajectories, but achieving performance beyond the teachers remains challenging. We propose a two-stage post training framework for flow-based embodied models, constructing distillation objectives from the velocity regression formulation of conditional flow matching. Stage 1 efficiently consolidates expert capabilities through MOPD. Stage 2 combines RL with teacher distillation that weights velocity errors according to the sampling noise, where distillation is restricted to failed trajectories to supplement sparse rewards with dense guidance without directly constraining successful behaviors. Experiments across multiple models and benchmarks show that the framework outperforms joint SFT and exceeds the corresponding teachers' aggregate success rates. Sample efficiency comparisons show higher success rates than direct RL with fewer environment interactions.

title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators on Locally Finite Trees
authors: Chenghao Xiang, Fayou Zhao
abstract: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, $\mathcal{N}^γ$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$, on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp $\ell^p \to \ell^q$ boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^γ$ and the triangular maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^γ$ on a prototypical tree, proving that the former's region strictly contains the latter's for all $0 < γ\leq 1$.

title: BendGS: Observation-Conditioned Gaussian Self-Modeling for Continuum Robots
authors: Jeong Woon Lee, Doungjun Kim, Namho Kim, Seungheon Chae, Jongwoo Kim, Hyoseok Hwang
abstract: Visual self-models learn from images how a robot moves under motor commands. Continuum robots need them even more, as they bend continuously without measured joint angles or fixed link geometry. Existing continuum self-models predict point clouds, image-space curves, or future images, but not the next 3D shape, appearance, and tip pose together from an observed body. 3D Gaussians offer a renderable representation of shape and appearance, yet articulated Gaussian self-models rely on joint angles to drive deformation. In this work, we propose BendGS, which uses a virtual backbone estimated from observation to drive command-conditioned Gaussian deformation, enabling next-state prediction for continuum robots without measured joint angles. In Gaussian modeling, a feed-forward network reconstructs the robot as 3D Gaussians from multi-view images, and the backbone, a chain of coordinate frames, is fitted to back-projected depth points to estimate the bending state. In transition, a network predicts its change under a relative motor command to deform the bound Gaussians. The deformed Gaussians render the next images and the 3D shape, and the distal frame gives the tip pose. Training losses use RGB-D images and masks, without bending or tip labels. On simulated and real robots, BendGS achieves the lowest Chamfer distance, best image quality, and lowest tip errors among the compared methods.

title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding
authors: Bastian Loss, Ahmad Nimr, Gerhard Fettweis
abstract: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.

title: Gaze World Model
authors: Jiawen Zhang, Houze Yang, Xu Cao, Yifan Shen, Zhongyi Zhou, Steve Wong, Ismini Lourentzou, Inki Kim, James M. Rehg
abstract: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode. This relationship is subtle, however, since an event far across the frame may produce only a slight movement of the person's head or eyes. We therefore introduce the Gaze World Model (GWM), which co-trains latent scene prediction with person-conditioned gaze supervision on a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder; in our ablations, the latent prediction objective improves both shift detection and gaze localization. Given a video clip and the person's head box, GWM estimates gaze locations and detects gaze shifts in the observed clip, and forecasts future gaze and shifts from predicted scene features. To train and evaluate these tasks, we augment VideoAttentionTarget and ChildPlay with event-level gaze-shift annotations. GWM achieves state-of-the-art shift detection on these benchmarks, about 10 points higher in four-class AP than the strongest baseline, while remaining comparable to the strongest image-based models in gaze target estimation, and outperforms the compared baselines on future gaze localization and shift forecasting.

title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
authors: Dathi Rajasekhar, Thien-Tam Nguyen, Trung Bao Le
abstract: We propose Spectral Jet KAN (SJ-KAN) to reduce the cost of differentiation and the network complexity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. The input coordinates are embedded through Chebyshev bases whose spatial derivatives are known in closed form, and all differentiation matrices are computed once for the collocation points before training. A single linear layer compresses the Chebyshev bases into a few latent features, and a single nonlinear Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CKAN) layer maps these features to the physical variables. Because the basis derivatives are known in advance and the compression is linear, the spatial derivatives in the NS equations are carried through the network analytically by a fixed sequence of matrix products and elementwise operations. Automatic differentiation (AD) is used only in backpropagation, to compute the gradients of the loss with respect to the network weights. We examine three variants of SJ-KAN (JetKAN, JetKAN-F, JetKAN-H), which differ in how the output layer maps the latent features to the physical variables. All variants are tested on the Taylor-Green vortex and on the lid driven cavity at Reynolds numbers Re = 100, 1000, 5000 and 10,000. The results are compared with a KAN that uses AD (PIKAN) and with a standard PINN. The SJ-KAN variants reach comparable or better accuracy than both, with up to 47 times fewer parameters and up to 8.2 times faster training per epoch. SJ-KAN also solves the lid driven cavity flow at Re = 10,000 without any reference data and with fewer than 9,000 trainable parameters. These results show that analytic derivative propagation, a small spectral input layer and a single KAN layer give a faster and simpler solver than methods based on AD, also for flows at high Reynolds numbers.

title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
authors: Honghuai Fang
abstract: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane. When the Newton coefficients have analytic tails, the Borel transform is assembled from convergent sums of simple poles along geometric progressions, and for such sums the Stokes jump of the Laplace sum determines every pole and residue. For an infinite family of twist knots containing the figure-eight knot, a positive Markov kernel gives an exact formula for the remainder of the Newton series. With it we show that, near a root of the Alexander polynomial, the rescaled analytic interpolation converges to Gaussian and Scorer-type profiles, uniformly for complex values of the rescaled color, and we determine how fast the rank may grow before these limits change. Finally, continuation in $\log q$ produces a logarithmic monodromy whose coefficient is a convergent pairing of the same Borel residues that give the Stokes jump. For the figure-eight knot, the asymptotics of this coefficient are governed by the hyperbolic volume at every rank.

title: VG-GP: Uncertainty-Gated Visuo-Geometric Memory for Negative-Transfer-Resistant Grasp Adaptation
authors: Yonglong Zhang
abstract: Pretrained antipodal grasping networks generalize well to canonical shapes but frequently fail zero-shot on novel objects with irregular mass distributions, thin rims, or unfamiliar handles. While episodic experience memory adapts a frozen base policy without retraining, naive retrieval suffers from visual appearance bias, negative transfer from overriding working base grasps, and degenerate closed-loop acquisition. We present VG-GP, a plug-and-play Visuo-Geometric Gaussian Process memory framework for closed-loop $SE(2)$ residual grasp transfer. First, we fuse color-invariant surface-normal DINOv2 features, canonical $SE(2)$ gripper-aligned 3D local heightmaps, and contact-geometry descriptors under a product kernel with Automatic Relevance Determination (ARD) lengthscales learned strictly on source objects. Second, we model the joint posterior over the base grasp and candidate $SE(2)$ alternatives, overriding the base policy only when the joint-covariance Lower Confidence Bound (LCB) clears a risk-sensitive threshold. Third, an online counterfactual curation gate using single-record necessity and sufficiency interventions quarantines source experiences causing negative transfer. Fourth, we close the acquisition loop via Bayesian Expected Improvement (EI) over equal-budget $SE(2)$ probes. Across 42 disjoint YCB objects in ManiSkill3 (20 source, 12 development, 10 held-out test), VG-GP wraps a pretrained GR-ConvNet base policy and raises physical lift rate across all 22 unseen objects from 38.6% (34/88) to 53.4% (47/88) with zero regressions (+13 rescues, 0 losses; object-clustered 95% CI [+6.8%, +22.7%], exact McNemar $p = 0.00024$). On the 10 held-out objects, EI active acquisition reaches 45.0% (18/40 vs. 32.5% base, 5/7 of oracle headroom), achieves 55.0% probe divergence over passive fallback, and monotonically reduces epistemic uncertainty.

title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models
authors: Keyu He, Michael Li, Jiarui Liu, Mingqian Zheng, Koichi Onoue, Tongshuang Wu, Maarten Sap
abstract: The training of socially intelligent language models often relies on large language model (LLM) judges, which are expensive, noisy, and vulnerable to reward hacking. Multi-player social games offer a natural alternative: they require open-ended communication to coordinate with teammates and infer hidden roles, while their rules provide an objective outcome which can serve as a verifiable reward for training. Using three social games, we explore how much social intelligence Qwen3 models can acquire through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Results show that against a much stronger Gemma-3-27B model, SFT and RLVR raise the win rate of Qwen3-4B from 33% to 81% on the three trained games, and from 39% to 54% on three additional held-out games. In contrast, in-context strategies such as prompting improve the win rate of Qwen3-4B by only about 6 pp across the same games we train and evaluate on. Furthermore, we show that the gains from SFT and RLVR hold across the model sizes 1.7B, 4B, and 32B. Qualitative analyses of agent behavior show signs of stronger social intelligence; for example, trained agents tend to share information more openly, check each other's claims against public evidence, and coordinate their votes. More broadly, our results demonstrate that training LLMs on verifiable outcomes in social games can cultivate generalizable social behaviors, which offers a scalable path for building socially intelligent agents.

title: Fibered-knot braids and symplectic fake quadrics
authors: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, Sai-Kee Yeung
abstract: We construct aspherical symplectic four-manifolds with the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$ by summing ruled surfaces along braided multisections. For each $m\geq1$, we form two symplectic sums with the same gluing map in the chosen surface markings and normal framings, using a stabilized braid for the trefoil in one sum and for the torus knot $T(2,7)$ in the other. Both sums have integral first homology $({\mathbb Z}/2)^2\oplus{\mathbb Z}/(4m)$. Their fundamental groups admit respectively $36$ and $24$ epimorphisms onto $S_3$, so the sums are nonhomeomorphic. We also vary the gluing while keeping the multisections fixed. In each of five product, twisted, and hybrid cases, this gives an infinite sequence in which the first homology groups have strictly increasing finite orders. All but finitely many members of each sequence admit no complex structure.

title: Elastic polar oscillations and nuclear parameters
authors: Hajime Sotani
abstract: Owing to the elasticity of a neutron star, the shear and interface modes are excited, in addition to the fundamental, pressure, and gravity modes. While direct observations of the oscillation spectrum remain challenging, potential resonance signatures from these modes could be manifested in the precursors of short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron star mergers. If the oscillation spectrum is observed, this is a good opportunity to extract the physical properties through the technique of asteroseismology. In particular, we focus on the crustal elasticity and examine the $s$- and $i$-mode frequencies. We find that, for a given EOS specified by the nuclear saturation parameters, the radius-scaled $s$-mode frequencies and the mass-scaled $i$-mode frequencies can be expressed as a function of the stellar compactness, independently of the stiffness of the core EOS, at least when the EOS in a higher-density region can be characterized only by the specific constant sound velocity. Then, we could derive the fitting formula for the $s_i$-mode for $i=1-4$ and $i_1$-mode frequencies as a function of the stellar compactness and the combination of the incompressibility of symmetric nuclear matter, $K_0$, and the slope parameter for the nuclear symmetry energy, $L$. If the $s$- and/or $i$-mode oscillation frequencies were observed, one may get the relation between these properties by identifying the observed frequencies with specific modes, using our fitting formula, which offers useful insights into the nuclear saturation parameters and stellar properties. By combining the other observational data, it may be possible to narrow the parameter space of EOS parameters and stellar properties. We emphasize that this article summarizes the results presented in our previous studies and discusses their implications for neutron star seismology.

title: Sharp inequalities for fractional spherical maximal operators on finite graphs
authors: Shengzhe Lu, Qizhen Shen, Fayou Zhao
abstract: This paper presents a systematic study of (quasi-)norm bounds for the fractional spherical maximal operator $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ on finite connected graphs $G$. We establish sharp estimates for the operator norm of $M_{α,G}^{\circ}$ from $\ell^p(G)$ to $\ell^q(G)$ for $0 < p \leq q \leq \infty$, with explicit extremal values attained by complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$. We solve the corresponding extremal graph problem by showing that complete and star graphs are the unique maximizers of the operator norm in different parameter regimes. Additionally, we characterize graphs containing a universal vertex in terms of their operator norm. Finally, we analyze the spherical maximal operator $M^{\circ}_{G}$ on paths $P_n$, uncovering a clear divergence in the operator's behavior between odd and even lengths.

title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
authors: Nikolaos Nikolaou
abstract: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge. We also need to know whether a "new proof" is indeed new, whether a thousand generated proofs contain one idea or many, and where each sits relative to human mathematics. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. Following Hilbert's 24th problem and the identity-of-proofs problem, we ask how far apart two proofs of one theorem are, and what shape the proof space they inhabit has. We define 19 dissimilarity measures in 6 families (syntactic, structural, dependency & resource, semantic, information-theoretic, higher-categorical) and 10 desirable properties, which we argue are the conditions for safely optimising a measure. In a Curry-Howard kernel, 5 machine-checked proofs that the primes are infinite show that raw syntax cannot tell a rewrite from a new argument, that dependency-based and structural measures reproduce the intuitive ordering (Euclid rewritten < Goldbach < Furstenberg), and that semantic measures invert it: Furstenberg's topological proof produces exactly Euclid's witness. A replication in Lean 4/Mathlib (3 theorems, 19 proofs, 18 measures) confirms that dependency-closure measures track intuition best, and shows that equality of normal forms never holds between differently written versions of the same argument, that proofs by citation look unlike the arguments they cite, and that proof irrelevance cannot distinguish any two proofs. We argue for reporting dissimilarity as a multi-level profile, extend the measures to proofs of different theorems, and discuss uses, from detecting duplicated AI proofs and orchestrating prover agents to interpreting AI proofs via their nearest human-understandable counterparts. Code, Lean sources and data are released.

title: Intrinsic Soft Function in the Continuum and Physical Mass Limit from Lattice QCD
authors: Zhi-Chao Gong, Min-Huan Chu, Jun Hua, Xiangdong Ji, Andreas Schäfer, Jin-Xin Tan, Han-Zhang Wang, Wei Wang, Jian-Hui Zhang, Mu-Hua Zhang, Qi-An Zhang
abstract: The intrinsic soft function is a universal nonperturbative ingredient of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. Despite substantial progress in lattice QCD studies, a determination with simultaneous control of the continuum, physical-pion-mass, and infinite-momentum limits has remained unavailable. In this work we present the first lattice determination incorporating all these limits within large-momentum effective theory, extracting the intrinsic soft function from a light-meson form factor and quasi-TMD wave functions. A key advance is the use of power-counting-guided axial-vector interpolators, which substantially improve the signal and enable a direct calculation at the physical pion mass. Combined with results from six ensembles spanning four lattice spacings, this improvement allows a precise determination extending to $b_\perp\simeq1.1~\mathrm{fm}$, while remaining consistent with perturbative predictions at short distances. The resulting transverse-distance dependence exhibits an approximately exponential decay, with the decay rate being characterized by an effective scale $Λ\simeq0.7~\mathrm{GeV}$ at $μ=2~\mathrm{GeV}$, providing a quantitative benchmark for nonperturbative Wilson-line dynamics and essential input for precision TMD studies.

title: Stokes corners and the global structure of steady rotating waves in annular domains
authors: Quan Wang
abstract: We study steady rotating water waves in a planar annulus, in the model of radial gravity and constant vorticity introduced by Li and the author. The stream function is harmonic, and the free surface carries the Bernoulli condition $p_0^2|\nablaΨ|^2=Q_α(S)$ with $Q_α(R)=(R-r_-)(R-r_+)$. We first settle the crest shape. For $α\neqα_\pm$, every stagnation point lies on the circle $R=r_-$, and the surface forms a symmetric $120^\circ$ corner there. At $α=α_\pm$ the corner is a right angle. The same holds for limits of smooth solutions and, in the lower region, for overhanging waves. We then study the global bifurcation continuum. Its waves are monotone from crest to trough, and they always cross the laminar circle. Hence there is no secondary bifurcation, and the parameter stays above an explicit floor. The continuum ends in an extreme wave, overturns, or degenerates; the last case is excluded for $c_0>γ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$. An annular Nekrasov equation and an invariant Keady--Norbury cone give a slope bound below $90^\circ$ whenever the Nekrasov weight is nonnegative on the waves. A sharpened angular flow-force estimate keeps the troughs where this weight is nonnegative, for every $γ\in(0,1)$ above the floor. Hence, whenever $c_0>γ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$, the existence half of the Stokes conjecture holds: the continuum contains an extreme wave with a $120^\circ$ Stokes crest. In the remaining band $\sinh^2γ<c_0\leγ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$ the result is conditional: the continuum ends in such a wave unless its parameter degenerates to the value at which the effective gravity vanishes on the stagnation circle, and we cannot exclude this degeneration. We also show that the bifurcation is supercritical for every $γ\in(0,1)$.

title: Where Did My Tokens Go? Verifiable Token Billing for LLM Services
authors: Jiayuan Du, Yebo Feng, Lin Zhang, Konglin Zhu
abstract: Users of large language model (LLM) services receive token bills with limited evidence of which calls incurred their charges. In broker-mediated agent workflows, calls arise after authorization and billing evidence spans service domains. A bill can count one genuine receipt twice and omit another. Valid metering evidence can also be attributed to the wrong execution. We present \textsc{TokenProv}, which uses authenticated provider acceptances to establish settlement coverage and verify token charges. An authenticated causal history links runtime attempts to the signed policy, and jointly signed handoffs bind intent, dispatch, and acceptance to the same call. Handoffs submitted independently of the bill can reveal omitted calls. The auditor requires a one-to-one match between observable acceptances and settled receipts. For each acceptance, a common provider relation binds metered usage to the cache-dependent execution of the accepted input using the registered model and serving rules, and checks the charge under the pricing rule. To limit serving-path overhead, providers can use attested state transitions in trusted execution environments or defer proof generation until audit by committing to witnesses in receipts before settlement. The auditor recomputes the bill from the verified charges. We prove audit soundness relative to authenticated evidence. Across five models, \textsc{TokenProv} with signed provider receipts achieves 94.4--107.4\% of baseline throughput with 54--66\,ms of online non-LLM processing per request. In a separate eight-call replay, deferring scoped proofs reduces foreground protocol time from 1.20\,s to 8.65\,ms (99.28\%). The auditor rejects all 1,600 validly signed attack queries across 100 adaptive episodes.

title: SceneMemBench: A Benchmark for Scene Memory in Interactive Video World Models
authors: Yuheng Si, Linye Lyu, Jiawei Zhou, Lingyi Du, Nanfei Ye, Aobo Liu, Yu Liu, Yu Li, Cheng Zhuo
abstract: Interactive video world models generate navigable worlds frame by frame, but a persistent world requires previously observed scenes to remain recoverable as users move away and return. Existing memory evaluations, however, often focus on seen-view revisits and full rollouts, leaving cross-view scene recovery underexplored while entangling memory with trajectory-following errors and accumulated generation degradation. We introduce SceneMemBench, a benchmark for scene memory in interactive video world models. It evaluates two complementary dimensions: seen-view recall versus novel-view recovery, and controlled diagnosis versus end-to-end interaction. We introduce Continued Rollout from a shared ground-truth observation history, alongside Full Rollout over complete model-generated interactions. SceneMemBench contains 600 controlled trajectories across 33 Unreal Engine scenes and 60 Full Rollout cases, covering eight representative open- and closed-source models. We evaluate scene recovery along subject consistency, appearance fidelity, and geometric consistency. Results show that novel-view recovery is generally more challenging than seen-view recall, while model profiles under controlled histories can differ markedly from those observed in full interaction. Together, these findings reveal complementary failure modes obscured by seen-view revisits or end-to-end rollouts alone.

title: Modeling Lunar Power Harvesting and Battery Recharging In The Presence of Random Pointing Error
authors: Barış Dönmez, Yanni Jiwan-Mercier, Julien Magné, Guillaume Blanchette, Paolo Pino, Sébastien Loranger, Güneş Karabulut Kurt
abstract: In our work, we establish a lunar power beaming environment between a low-lunar orbiter and a circular solar panel mounted on top of a lunar vehicle located at the Lunar South Pole. Due to the random nature of the pointing errors, various upper bounds reflecting the severity of these errors are considered. Although harvested power is modelled stochastically in the literature, we extend this randomness to battery-storage analysis by deriving PDFs of state of charge, accumulated battery capacity and energy, and end-to-end efficiency for both battery charging modes. Then, our derivations are verified with extensive Monte Carlo simulations. Hence, our derivations provide a mathematical model that enables prediction and helps us understand the randomness of the corresponding variables. For the given pointing error levels, we quantify the differences between charging modes in these battery metrics. Our work explains the stochastic nature of these battery metrics in a realistic lunar environment. Regarding the end-to-end efficiency metric, which is the ratio of the stored electrical energy to the transmitted electrical energy, we observed that slow-charging efficiency is immune to pointing errors, and this mode can utilize only one-sixth of what the link can deliver under a mild pointing error.

title: Learning Compact State Abstractions for LLM Agents
authors: Yaswanth Chittepu, Raghavendra Addanki, Anup Rao, Branislav Kveton, Scott Niekum
abstract: LLM agents commonly use the full interaction history as a proxy for state, retaining all past observations and actions regardless of whether they remain relevant. We instead ask what information an agent actually needs to carry forward. We define agent state as a compact abstraction of interaction history that preserves the competence of a fixed reference agent, with the minimal such abstraction as the ideal. Because matching the reference agent's behavior is unnecessarily restrictive and difficult for black-box policies, we define sufficiency through task performance rather than behavior matching. We represent state abstractions as deterministic recursive programs and search over them using an LLM-guided genetic algorithm. Across ALFWorld and ScienceWorld, the learned abstractions preserve near-reference task success while reducing mean policy input by up to 71% and 57%, respectively. The resulting programs are directly inspectable, providing an explicit account of what information is retained, updated, and discarded during interaction.

title: A Calculus for Borrowability
authors: Yanning Chen, Fan Long, Ningning Xie
abstract: Borrowing grants temporary shared or exclusive access to a linear resource without transferring ownership. However, capturing borrowing in a type system poses two challenges: a lender, the reference a borrow was taken from, should remain a first-class value that can be moved, and regain its permission when a non-lexical borrow ends. We propose borrowability, an index on reference types that tracks how access permissions are lent across lifetimes while separating them from the owner's obligation to release the resource. A lender is then an ordinary value whose borrowability records its remaining access permissions and the lifetimes of its active borrows, recovering borrowed permissions in place when those lifetimes end. We formalize borrowability in the calculus $λ^{boρ}$, mechanize its semantic type soundness and memory safety proofs in Rocq using Iris, and show that our design rules out all 24 in-scope soundness issues reported against the Rust compiler.

title: A Generative AI Agent to Emulate Interactive Human-driven Vehicles for Automated Driving Testing in Urban Areas
authors: Jia Hu, Changjian Yu, Panqu Wang, Jaehyun So, Yang Chang, Xuerun Yan, Jintao Lai
abstract: Realistic modeling of human-driven vehicle (HDV) interactions is essential for automated driving safety testing in urban areas. Existing methods struggle to reproduce realistic safety-critical interactions involving high collision risk for the following reasons: they often assume full observability, overlooking interactions arising from occlusion. Driving styles are mainly characterized by vehicle maneuvers, limiting the diversity of safety-critical interaction behaviors. Moreover, learning signals from safety-critical interactions can be diluted by non-critical driving behaviors. To address these issues, we propose a generative AI agent to emulate interactive HDVs. The agent incorporates field-of-view modeling to account for driver visibility under occlusion and characterizes the interaction process using five metrics spanning its initial, intermediate, and final stages. It automatically learns diverse interaction styles through a dynamic mixture-of-experts network. Through residual reinforcement learning, the agent further refines generated trajectories to match the real-world distributions of safety-critical interaction characteristics. Experiments on the INTERACTION dataset show that our method reduces Jensen--Shannon divergence (JSD) by 39.9\%--87.1\% across five interaction characteristics compared with a state-of-the-art baseline. Our method achieves greater improvements of up to 87.1\% in final-stage interaction metrics, suggesting that it can reduce error accumulation in long-horizon trajectory generation. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each proposed component, particularly highlighting the importance of residual refinement. Generalization experiments show that our method approaches the performance of full training on unseen intersections with only one epoch of fine-tuning.

title: Byte Patches versus BPE at Matched Data: A Matched-Twin Comparison at 350M Parameters
authors: Asadullah Maliyawala, Andrej Lisal
abstract: We compare a MEGABYTE-style byte-patch Transformer with a 64-byte sliding local decoder (local64) to a matched byte-level 8k BPE decoder (BPE-8k) under identical raw bytes, document order, and approximately matched bytes per optimizer step: 350M parameters and 10 billion training bytes. Under matched-span document sliding (identical scored byte ranges), BPE-8k leads with relative gaps of -5.2%, -4.9%, -9.3% and -6.1% in bits per byte (overall, text, code, math; paired bootstrap). Downstream, CharBench equal fine-tuning favors local64 (53.7% vs 40.0%), fact200 favors BPE-8k (16.5% vs 7.0%), and PIQA (raw and length-normalized) and ARC-Easy length-normalized favor BPE-8k after Holm correction at alpha = 0.05; remaining tasks are ties. Evaluation pitfalls that changed conclusions include context-length extrapolation past the BPE training context, bits per token reported as bits per byte, and inconsistent byte denominators. Unlike controlled tokenizer studies that vary the subword tokenizer under a fixed token budget, or FLOP-controlled byte-model scaling studies, we hold the raw bytes, their order and the optimizer recipe fixed and ask whether a fixed-patch byte model can replace the tokenizer at all. Limits: one size, one seed, one 8k vocabulary fixed before the runs, and a known difference in embedding initialization between the twins.

title: Wiener-type criteria for parabolic equations with two-sided Gaussian bounds
authors: Pilgyu Jung, Seick Kim, Sungjin Lee
abstract: We establish sufficient and necessary Wiener-type criteria for boundary regularity of parabolic equations whose fundamental solutions satisfy two-sided Gaussian bounds. In particular, our sufficient criterion holds at the critical exponent in the Gaussian lower bound. For the heat equation, the resulting double-series criterion is equivalent to the classical Wiener criterion of Evans and Gariepy. Our results apply to divergence form equations with bounded measurable, possibly nonsymmetric coefficients, and to non-divergence form equations with coefficients in $\mathrm{DMO}_x$ (Dini mean oscillation in space), without requiring continuity in time.

title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz under Pointwise Commutation
authors: Feng Guo
abstract: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic convergence of the corresponding sparse moment--SOS hierarchy for polynomial matrix optimization. We also derive a criterion for finite convergence of moment relaxation and extraction of a global minimizer based on local flatness and consistency of the local representing matrix measures on overlapping variable blocks. Finally, we provide a sufficient construction of commuting decompositions through linear equations, using a reference polynomial matrix with a simple spectrum at some point.

title: A Well-Posed Fourth-Order Navier-Stokes Model for Image Inpainting: Theory, Order Selection, and Stripe Decomposition
authors: Yiwen Dou, Yiqiang Ding, Zhongyun Bao, Senyan Zhao
abstract: The Navier-Stokes (NS) inpainting model of Bertalmío, Bertozzi and Sapiro is the only transport-type paradigm among PDE-based methods, yet it has never received a systematic higher-order extension. We show that the obvious fourth-order correction is ill-posed, and we construct the corrected, well-posed model. In the vorticity-streamfunction formulation we add a gated fourth-order term whose sign is decisive: the backward form is a Perona-Malik-type anti-diffusion, Hadamard ill-posed and consistently harmful in experiments, whereas the forward form is uniformly parabolic, energy-stable and consistently beneficial. An order-dissipation principle, stating that odd orders are dispersive and even orders dissipative, singles out the fourth order as the lowest admissible one. Large missing blocks pose a separate problem, because the correction gate stays silent there; we answer it with stripe decomposition, a Telea base fill followed by interleaved slit-wise NS passes, which converts block damage into the structural-slit regime where the model excels. The device is base-agnostic, and its gains add to those of the forward correction. On three datasets, namely BSDS500, DIV2K and a classical Chinese painting benchmark, and on three damage types, namely cracks, blocks and text occlusion, the training-free model beats every classical baseline on every sample of structure-dominated damage, gains +1.02 dB PSNR over Telea on the full 42-image painting test set with a 42/42 per-sample win rate, matches the strongest recent PDE solvers within 0.4 dB while attaining the best perceptual quality of the entire PDE family, and runs at 4-16 s per image on a consumer GPU.

title: Defining the mathematical family tree with a minimal programming language
authors: Max Tegmark
abstract: I introduce MLISP, a Turing-complete language with nine single-character commands (a b c d f 0 i j k), and use it to define 88 mathematical structures and a family tree of 65 theories that they model, with three aims: Pedagogy: It presents the mathematical structures in a unified way, with standardized presentation tableaus that define them and axiomatized theories that describe them. Connections: It highlights how they are related in the family tree via added symbols, axioms, etc. While the full tree is obviously infinite, its lower parts naturally separate into six main branches: the relational branch, the algebraic branch, the logic branch, the number branch, the set branch and the continuum branch. Foundations: The definitions, key theorems and models of each entry are verified in Lean. Mathematical structures are defined as equivalence classes of presentations, which in a constructivist spirit are defined in a simple, explicit and self-contained way in standardized presentation tableaus with minimal human baggage. For finite structures, the generating functions are defined by lookup tables. For countably infinite ones, they are instead defined computationally using MLISP, since more complex languages such as Lean are massive overkill for rigorously defining standard arithmetic operations (for example, the program "jibjbfid" defines subtraction). An interactive version is available at https://tegmark.org/mathtree. The Lean code is public, also verifies the correctness of MLISP and includes 43% of the theorems from Mathlib 2026-10-11. \end{abstract}

title: SPARQL-Planned Single-Hop Traversal over a Live Knowledge Graph for Multi-Hop Question Answering
authors: Priyesh Vakharia, Masud Moshtaghi, Pratyay Banerjee, Nicholas Jedema, Amita Misra, Ankit Chadha
abstract: Semantic retrieval struggles with multi-hop question answering on both recall and precision: gold passages are buried among distractors that degrade the reader's answer, and retrieving them requires reasoning over the query rather than matching it. GraphRAG techniques expand semantic retrieval by connecting passages to graph nodes and performing one or more hops of expansion after initial retrieval. This improves recall, but multi-hop expansion becomes expensive and brings additional noise into the retrieved set. We break this tradeoff by \emph{interleaving} dense retrieval with knowledge-graph traversal for complex multi-hop questions. Dense retrieval locates the first relevant regions of the search space at good recall, while traversal of a pre-existing external KG (Wikidata) restores precision and improves recall by confirming retrieved passages against a reasoning path through the KG. To keep traversal both question-adaptive and reliable, we have an LLM plan it as code generation task for graph traversal in SPARQL format but \emph{parse rather than execute} the query. On full 1{,}000-question splits under a shared corpus and reader, and with a single configuration applied identically to every dataset, we reach \textbf{62.5 / 75.1} EM/F1 on HotpotQA, \textbf{73.5 / 81.0} on 2WikiMultiHopQA, and \textbf{37.1 / 50.0} on MuSiQue, ahead of reproduced HippoRAG2, T\textsuperscript{2}RAG, and IRCoT on all three benchmarks. A second, token-matched setting stays ahead of T\textsuperscript{2}RAG on HotpotQA and 2Wiki while spending roughly its per-query budget. Executing the generated SPARQL instead of parsing it costs up to 11.4 EM, mostly because raw queries return empty results, not because of syntax errors.

title: ET: Efficient Transfer from Softmax to Hybrid Attention
authors: Guangfu Guo, Xiaoqian Lu, Linsey Pang, Weiran Yao, Haolin Chen, Long Cheng, Kunpeng Liu
abstract: Converting pretrained softmax Transformers to efficient attention often causes substantial performance degradation, while recovery typically requires costly fine-tuning. We propose ET (Efficient Transfer), a framework for high-fidelity attention conversion with minimal optimization cost. ET combines exact local and shared-key softmax attention with a mean-anchored, scan-free global linear correction and adaptive gating, achieving linear complexity in sequence length. To preserve pretrained knowledge, ET freezes pretrained weights and calibrates only newly introduced parameters through alternating least squares on a small set of unlabeled samples, without gradient updates. On ImageNet-1K, ET achieves 79.64% and 81.55% top-1 accuracy on DeiT-S and DeiT-B, respectively, within 0.25 percentage points of their softmax teachers. At $768\times768$, ET outperforms T$^5$ by 3.59 percentage points at comparable inference FLOPs, without gradient-based fine-tuning. On DiT-XL/2, ET achieves an FID-50K of 2.59 with only 250 LoRA updates. On Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium, ET matches the teacher's GenEval score at 1K resolution with just 0.73 A100 GPU-hours of gradient-free conversion and a 1.39$\times$ inference speedup.

title: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset
authors: Yizhak Ben-Shabat, Jiahao Zhang, Joseph Liu, Seonghyeon Moon, Young-Yoon Lee, Haomiao Jiang, Oren Jacob, Mubbasir Kapadia
abstract: While text-driven body motion generation has matured, pure-hand synthesis remains bottlenecked by data. Existing datasets often treat hands as rigid end-effectors, lack fine-grained captions, or are too limited in scale to support robust generalization. We introduce RoMo Hands, an in-the-wild, text-paired dataset of ~542K sequences (884 hours, 95.5M frames at 30 fps) which is an order of magnitude larger than prior work. To ensure high-quality supervision, a stringent dexterity filter discards low-articulation sequences, focusing the distribution on complex bimanual movement. Each clip is paired with five captions at increasing granularities from global semantic tags to atomic finger states, organized under a hierarchical taxonomy. To bridge the gap between body and hand architectures, we propose a novel 393-D bimanual representation that adapts redundant body-motion paradigms to the high-DoF kinematics of hands. Systematic benchmarking of diffusion, masked-token, and autoregressive generators reveals distinct trade-offs under these hand-specific adaptations, including a sharp divergence between semantic alignment and kinematic plausibility. Our dataset, representation, and benchmark establish a rigorous foundation for the next generation of dexterous motion synthesis. Project page: https://romodataset.github.io/romo-hands/.

title: Verified Proof Refactoring with Codex and Qwen
authors: Lazar Milikic, Gordan Đurić, Viktor Kunčak
abstract: We refactor existing Lean 4 proofs to reduce source length and checking cost while preserving theorem statements and compatibility across Lean versions. A locally served Qwen model uses the open-source Codex CLI to inspect source, retrieve declarations, and test proof replacements. The host keeps a replacement only if it improves the objective and Lean accepts it on every required version. A deterministic CPU pass then refines the verified proofs. On the 60 problems in Lean Refactor Arena, model search achieves a local mean combined score of 82.07, and cleanup raises it to 82.18. The final proofs pass all 127 required proof--version checks. Our system placed first in the open-source LLM track of Lean Refactor Arena at VeriCodeGen.

title: A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies
authors: Vicente Aguilar, Fabrizio Canfora, Vicente García, Alex Giacomini, Julio Oliva
abstract: We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $Λ_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.

title: Xtream: An Explicit Metric State for Large-Scale Streaming Reconstruction
authors: Ernesto Lozano, Alberto Jaenal, Javier Civera
abstract: 3D foundation models (3DFMs) enable dense reconstruction in a feed-forward pass, yet their effective span is limited by cross-view attention. Local consistency has been expanded through geometric alignment of video chunks and recursive updates of an implicit memory, and large-scale scenes with pose graphs. However, both strategies are prone to drift, largely due to the lack of metric-scale observability from monocular geometry. We present Xtream,a hybrid streaming pipeline that maintains an explicit metric state through a factor graph over keyframes, while using a 3DFM as a geometric front end. Xtream incorporates metric information in two ways: through metric scale predictions from 3DFMs; or through inertial measurements if available. Across the large-scale benchmarks of VBR, Oxford Spires and KITTI, Xtream achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3DFM-based online reconstruction, reducing average absolute trajectory errors compared with published baselines and concurrent work. https://ernestolozano.github.io/xtream

title: RVLM-X: Towards a Universal VLM Harness
authors: Aadi Palnitkar, Dmytro Kurdydyk, Xiaomin Lin
abstract: Harnesses for vision-language models (VLMs) have grown with the models' capabilities, notably for images far larger than those seen in training, where downscaling loses small details. Most of them wrap the VLM in a fixed procedure, such as a zoom tree, that decides in advance where it looks and how the evidence is combined. These procedures make up for the weaknesses of older models by keeping them on a task-specific path, but with frontier models that reliably plan and use tools, they can lower accuracy. We propose RVLM-X, a task-generalizable recursive VLM harness that runs unchanged across photographs, charts and maps. Following the recursive inference of Recursive Language Models, the VLM programmatically controls its own visual context in a code REPL that holds the full-resolution image and calls itself recursively on regions that it chooses. With a cost-efficient frontier model as the base of every method, RVLM-X is more accurate than a single call on all 7 public benchmarks and has the highest pooled accuracy. Because existing benchmarks mostly test whether a model finds one small detail, we also introduce MapGenBench, procedurally generated maps whose questions combine fine-detail perception with multi-step reasoning. There, RVLM-X answers 71.4% of held-out questions against 55.5% for the strongest baseline. Overall, our findings suggest that as VLMs plan and use tools more reliably, letting the model write its own visual search works better than fixing one in advance.

title: On equational $\mathfrak{X}$-domains
authors: Omar Al-Raisi, Mohammad Shahryari
abstract: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups containing all abelian groups. We introduce and investigate equational $\X$-domains as a generalization of equational domains in algebraic geometry over groups. We characterize these groups by means of systems of equations associated with the identities of $\X$, and describe the radical and coordinate group of the union of two coordinate axes. We also extend classical characterizations of coordinate groups of irreducible algebraic sets, involving discrimination and universal theories, to the setting of equational $\X$-domains. Finally, we establish two construction results: under suitable malnormality, amalgamated free products are equational $\X$-domains; moreover, a restricted regular wreath product of two nontrivial groups is an equational $\X$-domain if and only if its base group is an equational $\X$-domain.

title: Density elimination for weakly commutative pseudo-uninorm logic:a correction and an explicit theory-level completeness proof
authors: SanMin Wang
abstract: We correct the density-elimination argument for weakly commutative pseudo-uninorm logic in Wang, \emph{Symmetry} 11 (2019), 368, retaining its basic ideas and overall strategy. The published definition of a labelled copy permits independent renamings of antecedent and succedent labels. Under the syntactic splicing interpretation used in that argument, a contraction-free derivable hypersequent and a four-element residuated chain refute the claimed compatibility of the resulting contraction with ordered density elimination. We require a single renaming on both sides of each closed block and prove that the linear rules and coherent closed-block contraction preserve provability of every member of the associated Cartesian families. An occurrence-based separation argument, together with normalization to cuts on the monoidal unit, establishes strong density elimination. We then derive standard completeness from density, retaining the original conclusion for formula theorems. For an explicit Hilbert presentation with independent conjugation parameters, we give a direct relative chain-countermodel proof for arbitrary theories in a countable language. Combined with the full bounded embedding of Wang (2026), this recovers the corresponding strong standard completeness result already stated there. The distinguished constant $f$, when present, is interpreted independently of the monoidal unit and the lattice bounds. The main results of this paper have been formally verified in Lean~4.

title: Hadron structure in $1+1$ dimensions from the infinite Hamiltonian lattice
authors: Ross Dempsey
abstract: The internal structure of a hadron is encoded in matrix elements of operators between hadron states of definite momentum. In this paper, we develop a framework for computing such matrix elements in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories by working on an infinite spatial lattice. We apply the method to the massive Schwinger model. We benchmark our method against discretized lightcone quantization (DLCQ) at $θ= 0$, and then use the lattice to study hadrons at $θ\neq 0$, where DLCQ does not apply. We compute parton distribution functions and gravitational form factors, and both show signatures of hadrons becoming large, loosely-bound states when we set $m$ greater than the critical mass $m_c$ and approach $θ= π$ from below. Moreover, we see the gravitational form factor change from that of a free boson to that of a free Majorana fermion when we set $θ= π$ and approach the 2D Ising critical point at $m=m_c$ from below.

title: A unified stochastic random walk theory for Kolmogorov spectrum, halo mass functions, and halo density profiles
authors: Zhijie Xu
abstract: We develop a unified stochastic framework for nonequilibrium systems and apply it to turbulence and cosmic structure formation. Spectra and distributions evolve by transport in "scale space", described by random walks and Fokker-Planck equations with scale-dependent waiting times. We reformulate the turbulent cascade as a random walk in wavenumber space with waiting time $τ_{gk}\propto k^{-γ}$. With $γ=2/3$ fixed by self-consistency, we recover the Kolmogorov $-5/3$ law and obtain the full energy spectrum, including the inertial-dissipation crossover, exponential cutoff and spectrum constant, without applying dimensional analysis to the spectrum itself. In bottom-up hierarchical structure formation, low-mass haloes collapse early and retain primordial imprints, while prolonged assembly near the characteristic mass $m_h^*$ erases this memory and establishes a universal spectrum $P(k)\propto k^{-1}$. We model this as a random walk in halo mass space with $τ_g\propto m_h^{-λ}$. This yields a stretched Gaussian halo mass function that reproduces the Press-Schechter form, with small-scale scaling $f_M\propto m_h^{-λ}$ and an exponential cutoff at $m_h>m_h^*$, both set by $λ$. It also produces a double-$λ$ mass function: $λ$ reflects the primordial spectrum at low masses and approaches $2/3$ near $m_h^*$, where gravity dominates. For individual haloes, a spatial random walk with $τ_{gr}\propto r^{-γ}$ generates a double-$γ$ density profile that reproduces the Einasto profile, with small-scale scaling $ρ_r\propto r^{-2γ}$ and an exponential cutoff at $r>r_s$, both set by $γ$. Here $γ$ is fixed by the initial spectrum in the inner core and approaches $2/3$ ($ρ_r\propto r^{-4/3}$) in the gravity-dominated outskirts. This framework thus describes turbulent cascades and cosmic structure formation on a common footing.

title: Mechanisms of turnkey soliton generation in self-injection-locked photonic-crystal ring resonators
authors: Naoya Kuse
abstract: Turnkey generation of dissipative Kerr solitons in photonic-crystal ring resonators relies on the interplay between engineered mode splitting, self-injection locking, and modulation instability, yet the mechanism governing soliton initiation and number selection remains incompletely understood. We investigate this interplay using coupled Lugiato-Lefever equations with a self-consistent nonlinear self-injection-locking condition. Analysis of continuous-wave steady states and their locking stability reveals operating points accessible through feedback-induced transitions between split resonances. Evaluating modulation-instability gain at these points identifies conditions for comb initiation and links the dominant unstable sideband modes to soliton-number selectivity. Direct time-domain simulations corroborate the analysis, showing that appropriately chosen mode splitting enables highly repeatable single-soliton generation without external laser-frequency scans. The final soliton number is nevertheless shaped by subsequent nonlinear evolution and feedback-induced detuning changes, rather than by the initial instability alone. We also show that larger dispersion suppresses higher-order unstable modes and favors lower soliton numbers.

title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
authors: Xuefeng Liu
abstract: The inf-sup constant $β(Ω)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $β$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $β$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $β$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1π$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\leβ\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\leβ\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\leβ\le0.154781$. For the rectangles $(0,1)\times(0,r)$ we enclose $β$ for eight aspect ratios and prove for the five ratios $r\in\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac12,\frac9{16},\frac58\}$ that $β^2$ is an isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum; the last two lie beyond the range covered by the explicit bound of Costabel, Crouzeix, Dauge and Lafranche. As an application, the certified values give guaranteed a posteriori bounds for Taylor--Hood approximations of the Stokes equations, including the doubly connected domain, for which, to our knowledge, no explicit lower bound for $β$ had been available.

title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
authors: Zheyu Zhou
abstract: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations. For two arrivals with binary valuations and every $k\ge2$, the optimal fraction is $1/p$, where $p$ is the largest integer with $1+\binom{2p}{2}\le k$. In particular, up to six binary types permit full maximin share. For two arbitrary additive types, a different polynomial-time algorithm guarantees $4/7$ of maximin share for any number of agents. This ratio is tight for the algorithm. With three arrivals and two types, the optimal deterministic fraction is exactly $9/10$. For randomized policies with $k$ known additive types, the optimal MMS fraction guaranteed to all agents with probability at least $1-δ$ on every fixed arrival sequence is $Θ(\max\{k^{-1/2},\sqrtδ\})$ for $0\leδ<1$.

title: Sharp Hellinger Risk of the Multivariate Gaussian NPMLE
authors: Xingzhou Wang, Zheng Li
abstract: For multivariate Gaussian location mixtures whose mixing distributions have coordinatewise sub-Gaussian tails, we prove that the unconstrained nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator attains the minimax rate $(\log n)^d/n$ under squared Hellinger loss. This holds for every fixed dimension $d\geq2$ and every fixed tail parameter $σ>0$. The upper bound applies to every measurable choice of a global likelihood maximizer and improves the earlier bound of order $(\log n)^{d+1}/n$ by a factor of $\log n$. A key step is a sharp bracketing bound for multivariate polynomials. For the $L^2(ρ)$ unit ball of real polynomials in $d$ variables with total degree at most $m$, the log bracketing number at width $\varepsilon$ is at most $\binom{m+d}{d}\log(C_d/\varepsilon)$ for $0<\varepsilon\leq1$. The constant $C_d$ depends only on $d$. The bound holds for every positive Borel measure $ρ$ under which each nonzero polynomial in the space has a finite, positive $L^2(ρ)$ norm. We prove the bound using volume estimates for a complex Veronese cone and Gaussian small-ball probabilities, then apply it to bound the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of Gaussian mixture densities. We obtain the matching minimax lower bound by adapting the Hermite perturbation construction of Kim and Guntuboyina.

title: Denotational Results in Compiler Correctness and Comparisons with Operational Approaches
authors: Jeremy G. Siek, Matthew Heimerdinger, Tianyu Chen, Darshal Shetty
abstract: Anyone setting out to prove a compiler correct must choose a style of semantics. The CakeML and CompCert projects, among others, show that operational semantics such as abstract machines and interpreters are viable choices. In this paper we explore whether denotational semantics can also be used in proofs of compiler correctness and evaluate the tradeoffs. We focus on a compiler from FPC, a language with lexically scoped functions and recursive types, to a first-order low-level intermediate language. This compiler includes closure conversion, but no prior proof of correctness with respect to denotational semantics covers closure conversion for a Turing-complete language. Compiler correctness requires that the denotation of a program be both preserved and reflected by the compiler. For closure conversion, reflection is the hard direction. We present the first denotational proofs of semantic reflection for closure conversion applied to a Turing-complete language, one proof with respect to a graph model and one with respect to Scott domains. For the graph-model proof we develop a new logical relation, the approximant logical relation, and for the Scott-domain proof we adapt a logical relation of Reynolds. As a first step in evaluating the tradeoffs, we compare mechanized correctness proofs of an eight-pass compiler, from FPC down to a typed low-level intermediate language, in five semantic styles. Two of the styles are denotational and three are operational. We find that no one semantics yields the shortest proofs for every compiler pass. We identify two factors that influence proof size. For operational semantics, proof size tends to grow with how much the runs of the source and target differ. For denotational semantics, the proofs are succinct when the correctness of a pass is an equation between meanings, and lengthy when a pass needs a logical relation.

title: EventSSM: Causal Spatial-State Modelling for Asynchronous Events Event-Depth Estimation
authors: Sadiq O. Macaulay, Dipon Ghosh, Hadfield Simon
abstract: Event cameras report asynchronous brightness changes, yet metric-depth supervision is typically available only at sparsely sampled reference timestamps. Aggregating events into frame-like representations simplifies learning but can obscure the fine-grained temporal structure of the original event stream. We introduce EventSSM, a causal spatial-state framework for event-associated metric-depth estimation using a recurrent memory updated by chronological event packets. To bridge asynchronous predictions and frame-time supervision, predicted event depths are geometrically transported using calibrated camera poses and differentiably rendered at reference timestamps. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate improvements over established event-depth methods across multiple depth-error measures. Controlled ablations further examine cross-modal initialization, temporal recurrence, individual state, readout, and supervision components, and packet subdivision. Together, these findings establish EventSSM as an effective framework for causal event-associated metric-depth estimation, combining persistent spatial context with physically timed state retention.

title: Theory of modulation instability for coupled microresonators
authors: Alena Kolesnikova, Andrey Gelash
abstract: Thanks to hybridization phenomena, coupled microresonator systems enable modulation instability (MI) of the continuous wave background field across all possible dispersion combinations: anomalous-anomalous, normal-normal, and anomalous-normal microrings. Here, using the Lugiato-Lefever model in the supermode basis for two coupled microresonators with arbitrary second-order dispersion coefficients, arbitrary losses, and coupling strength, we derive a general eigenvalue problem for the $4\times 4$ matrix. We consider the regime of resonance splitting, in which the pump couples only to one of the two supermodes, allowing us to obtain analytical expressions for the stationary continuous-wave field distributed over the coupled system. When the microresonators have similar geometry, the antidiagonal elements of the eigenvalue-problem matrix nearly vanish, and we obtain a fully analytical solution for the MI gain rate for the entire range of coupled microresonator devices. Finally, we investigate cases in which the analytical treatment must be supplemented with more accurate numerical solutions of the MI eigenvalue problem, though even then the analytical theory captures the main features of the four-wave mixing process and the gain-rate behavior.

title: DUALingo: A Dual-Hand Instruction-Guided Dataset for Affordance Grounding on 3D Objects
authors: Ming-Lun Lee, Yi-En Li, Feng-Dian Su, Ming-Han Lee, Kun-Ru Wu, Krzysztof Czarnecki, Yu-Chee Tseng
abstract: Affordance grounding localizes where an agent should interact with an object to perform a task. Many everyday manipulation tasks, however, require bimanual affordance, in which two hands assume complementary and cooperative roles to accomplish a shared goal. Existing 3D affordance datasets primarily ground single interaction regions, and manually annotating dual-hand, cooperative contacts does not scale. To address this gap, we introduce DUALingo, a large-scale dataset for task-conditioned, role-aware bimanual 3D affordance grounding on diverse everyday objects. DUALingo represents each task as two cooperative, hand-agnostic roles, each grounded as a heatmap on the object surface. It contains 271K free-form tasks on 71K objects, generated by a fully automated pipeline of open-weight foundation models without human labeling. Expert ratings and a validated LLM judge confirm the quality of the resulting annotations. Trained on DUALingo, existing 3D affordance models learn to ground both cooperative roles from natural-language instructions, with the best-performing model achieving a more than threefold improvement in aIoU over the zero-shot baseline, from 10.3 to 37.8. Robotic manipulation demonstrations illustrate the actionability of the predicted bimanual affordances in performing cooperative tasks. These results position DUALingo as a scalable foundation for learning everyday bimanual affordances. Project page: https://nycu-pair-labs.github.io/DUALingo/

title: ReJEPA: Bounded Predictive Regulation for Latent World Models
